articles.title: Sinner to miss Australian Open after undergoing surgery on knee injury
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open in January after surgery for a persistent knee injury, Tennis Australia confirmed. The world No. 2 has been sidelined since winning Wimbledon in July and had initially expected to return for Melbourne. Italian media reported he could be out for up to four months, but that longer estimate has not been confirmed by his team.

articles.title: Nyk Lewis' late jumper lifts VCU past Washington in Maui
articles.summary: VCU beat Washington 80–78 in the Maui Invitational after Nyk Lewis hit a driving jumper with 1.8 seconds left. The Rams erased a 10-point second-half deficit with an 8–1 closing run; Washington’s Nikola Dzepina scored a career-high 31 points but missed a final long-range attempt. VCU improved to 5–2, while 17 Washington turnovers helped decide the game.

articles.title: Behind Alex Tuch's big night, Capitals best Flyers, end 5-game skid
articles.summary: Washington defeated Philadelphia 7–3, ending a five-game losing streak and handing the Flyers their first loss in four games. Alex Tuch scored once and assisted twice, while seven Capitals found the net and Logan Thompson made 18 saves. The teams traded early goals before Washington took control in the second period and added late insurance. The result was the Capitals’ second win over Philadelphia this season.

articles.title: India orders tougher surveillance of packaged water, scrutiny set to cover PepsiCo, Coca-Cola
articles.summary: India’s food regulator ordered states to intensify inspections and risk-based sampling of packaged and mineral water after a Bisleri sample was flagged as unsafe. Reuters reports checks will also cover PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Tata Consumer and Reliance Consumer in a market worth about $3.5 billion. Bisleri says its own testing found no problem; the regulator says it plans prosecution over alleged non-compliance.

articles.title: Apple pulls MiniMax AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
articles.summary: Apple removed MiniMax’s Talkie chatbot from its App Store worldwide after reports that AI characters sent sexually inappropriate or abusive messages to minors. Reuters says the app was rated for adults but relied partly on self-reported ages, raising questions about safeguards. Talkie had about 11 million monthly active users in October and was once a major revenue source for MiniMax; Apple and the company had not commented.

articles.title: Turkmenistan's Afghan gas link brings South Asia pipeline dream a little closer
articles.summary: Turkmenistan expects to finish a gas-pipeline section to Afghanistan’s Herat by year-end, with flows planned for early 2027. The segment is part of the proposed 1,800-kilometre TAPI route to Pakistan and India, designed for 33 billion cubic metres annually. Reuters reports only 124 kilometres of the Afghan section have been laid; financing, security and India-Pakistan tensions still threaten the wider project.

articles.title: Spain's economic gains miss voters' wallets as Sanchez seeks reelection
articles.summary: Spain's economy is growing faster than the euro zone and creating jobs, but many voters say the gains have not eased housing and living-cost pressures ahead of Sunday's snap election. Reuters reports growth is uneven across regions and social classes, leaving frustration despite strong headline data. Polls suggest Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's Socialists trail the conservative People's Party, which may need Vox to govern.

articles.title: EU leaders to wrestle with seven-year budget, Ukraine financing as they seek December deal
articles.summary: EU leaders are debating a proposed €1.582 trillion budget for 2028–34 and a €45 billion joint loan for Ukraine, which would be repaid only if Russia pays reparations. The plan also includes up to €100 billion for Ukraine over the seven-year period. Reuters reports several member states oppose the loan, while the bloc hopes to reach a budget deal in December.

articles.title: BOJ's Tamura signals chance of faster-pace interest rate hikes
articles.summary: Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said the central bank should move its policy rate toward a neutral level soon and could accelerate increases if inflation overshoots. He cited higher oil and raw-material costs, broadening wholesale price pressures, yen volatility and strong AI-related demand. Tamura said firms appear able to absorb past hikes, but his comments do not represent a board decision or guarantee a faster schedule.

articles.title: South Korea's central bank raises rates, upgrades 2027 growth outlook
articles.summary: The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 point to 3.25%, citing inflation and financial-stability risks as semiconductor exports surge. It raised its 2026 growth forecast to 3.9% and 2027 to 4.1%, while October inflation was 2.8%. Household debt reached a record 2,030 trillion won, and two of seven policy-board members preferred holding rates at 3%, AP reported.

articles.title: Black Friday? No thanks, some brands say
articles.summary: Some brands are opting out of Black Friday to protect margins, push back against constant discounting or signal sustainability values. Italian fashion brand Pinko estimates the decision will cost about €2 million in revenue but says the profit hit is smaller. Analysts say discount fatigue and distrust of advertised savings make the strategy risky, though it can help retailers stand out.

articles.title: No. 18 USC rallies, then holds on to edge South Carolina
articles.summary: No. 18 Southern California stayed unbeaten at 7–0 by rallying past South Carolina 71–69 in the Acrisure Series. Alijah Arenas scored 25 points, including 12 of 13 free throws, as USC closed on a 10–2 run and held the Gamecocks scoreless for the final 4:05. South Carolina led by as many as 10 but missed two late go-ahead shots.

articles.title: Judge temporarily blocks FCC from early license review of ABC
articles.summary: A federal judge granted ABC a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction blocking the FCC's early review of eight Disney-owned stations, finding the network likely to succeed on its First Amendment retaliation claim. The review followed President Trump's call for ABC to fire Jimmy Kimmel. The judge declined to bar unspecified future FCC actions; the agency says it will continue enforcing broadcasters' public-interest duties.

articles.title: Stocks rally in Asia, US tariffs not as dire as feared
articles.summary: European shares rebounded 1.4% Thursday as banks and technology stocks recovered, extending an Asia-led market bounce. Investors judged proposed U.S. tariffs may be less severe than feared, with EU duties likely capped at the previously agreed 15% rate. The move followed a sharp selloff driven by inflation, interest-rate and AI-growth concerns; market direction remains sensitive to policy details and earnings expectations.

articles.title: Indonesian rescuers resume search for 13 people trapped inside illegal mine after 13 confirmed dead
articles.summary: Rescuers in West Java planned to resume searching for 13 workers trapped in an illegal gold mine after 13 of the 26 miners who entered Monday were confirmed dead. Heavy rain flooded the shaft about 100 metres underground. Six victims had been identified; narrow, slippery access and weather complicate the operation. Authorities say the site was unauthorized and unrelated to state miner Antam.

articles.title: Data centre rush drives biggest rise in Australian business investment since mining boom
articles.summary: Australian private capital spending rose 12.2% in the September quarter to A$59.5 billion, its biggest increase since 2011 and well above forecasts. Spending on information and telecommunications equipment jumped 87% as firms bought data-centre servers and processing gear, much of it imported. Businesses also raised planned investment for 2026–27, suggesting technology demand is resilient even as higher rates weigh on households.

articles.title: Liberal senator Leah Blyth defects to One Nation in major blow for Angus Taylor
articles.summary: South Australian Liberal senator Leah Blyth defected to One Nation, becoming the party's first federal senator from the state and dealing a blow to opposition leader Angus Taylor. Blyth said she had lost confidence in the Liberals' ability to address immigration, spending and energy policy. Former colleagues accused her of self-interest; she said she had not discussed the move with them beforehand.

articles.title: Australia's emissions fall but not fast enough to reach 2035 climate target
articles.summary: Australia's greenhouse-gas emissions fell 1.3% in the year to June 2026, but the Climate Change Authority says the pace must accelerate to meet the country's 2030 and 2035 targets. Renewables supplied a record 45.9% of electricity in the national market, while transport emissions edged up. Advisers estimate annual cuts of 25–30 million tonnes are needed over the next nine years.

articles.title: Emailed bomb threat against NT government ministers and public areas under investigation by NT Police
articles.summary: Northern Territory police are investigating an encrypted email threatening ministers, government staff and public places in Darwin. Police said specialist units were assessing the message and would treat it as credible until checks were complete; officials urged residents to remain alert but not alarmed. The sender's identity is unknown, and authorities have withheld specific targets while the investigation continues.

articles.title: Government gives environmental green light to Western Downs Digital Park
articles.summary: Australia's federal environmental regulator ruled that the proposed A$32 billion Western Downs Digital Park in Queensland does not need further federal assessment, finding it unlikely to significantly affect nationally protected matters. The project, backed by Anthropic, would be Australia's largest proposed data centre, but still needs state and local approvals. Critics warn its power demand could create major emissions if not supplied by renewables.

articles.title: Kurtley Beale back in Wallabies gold for Ireland Test, Allan Alaalatoa to make 100th appearance
articles.summary: Kurtley Beale, 37, has been named on Australia's bench for its Nations Championship Test against Ireland, marking his first Wallabies selection since 2021. Coach Les Kiss said the veteran earned the place through performance and versatility, not as a farewell gesture. Allan Alaalatoa will earn his 100th cap and winger James Ramm is set for his international debut.

articles.title: Blue groper Ziggy missing after suspected Mollymook speargun attack
articles.summary: A protected eastern blue groper known locally as Ziggy has not been seen since being found with serious injuries consistent with a speargun attack near Mollymook, New South Wales. The fish is estimated to be over 30 years old and had been a familiar presence for snorkellers. Local conservation groups plan to seek warning signs; authorities have been contacted, and no suspect has been identified.

articles.title: Weather bureau predicts hot Australian summer across the board
articles.summary: Australia's Bureau of Meteorology expects above-average summer temperatures across almost the entire country as El Niño strengthens. October was the warmest on record at 1.05°C above the 1961–1990 average. The outlook also points to drier conditions in parts of the west and south, but heavier rain risk in southern Queensland and northeastern New South Wales, with flash flooding possible.

articles.title: Taxpayer-funded cleaners charging up to $135 per hour face aged care restrictions
articles.summary: Australian pensioners say rules for the Support at Home program leave subsidised cleaners unable to move chairs, bend down or reach high surfaces, even when clients pay substantial hourly fees. ABC found some clients were billed up to A$135 an hour while workers received A$32–36. Providers cite safety and liability rules; a Senate inquiry is due to report next year.

articles.title: Oil little changed as supply concerns linger after Iran claims mine strikes on ships
articles.summary: Crude was little changed Thursday after a sharp prior-session rise: Brent slipped 0.1% to $94.52 a barrel while WTI gained 0.2% to $83.83. Traders weighed Houthi claims of an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and Iranian reports of tanker mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. The reported mine incidents were not independently verified; OPEC+ ministers meet November 29 on 2027 output policy.

articles.title: US officials divided over Chinese spying allegations following Jensen Huang's return
articles.summary: Reuters reports U.S. agencies disagree over what intelligence shows about Alice Huang, a former executive at an Nvidia customer company who had contact with China's Ministry of State Security. The FBI's assessment reportedly found no evidence she was an intelligence officer or asset; the CIA said available reporting did not establish she passed sensitive information, while leaving room for new evidence. The accounts are based on people briefed on classified material; China denies the espionage allegations.

articles.title: Musk says every U.S. child will receive two SpaceX shares
articles.summary: Elon Musk said every U.S. child would receive two SpaceX shares—one newly issued by the company and one donated by him—after SpaceX said it would contribute a share to each active Trump Account. The company has not clarified whether Musk's shares would follow the same eligibility rules or carry sale restrictions. The proposal builds on earlier share-gifting pledges, but key distribution details remain unresolved.

articles.title: Trump and NATO chief urge Russia not to widen Ukraine war
articles.summary: President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte urged Russia not to take actions that could widen the war in Ukraine, after meeting in Florida. Their joint statement also cited a need for a rapid peaceful resolution and discussed defense spending and investment, but offered no details on talks about the Iran war. European allies continue to press for a role in U.S.-backed peace negotiations.

articles.title: Kenya government breached constitution in building US-backed Ebola quarantine site, court says
articles.summary: A Kenyan court ruled that the government breached constitutional provisions when constructing a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility and ordered work to stop until conditions are met, including disclosure of the agreement with Washington. The ruling adds legal and transparency hurdles to a project intended for outbreak response; Reuters did not report when construction could resume.

articles.title: Data from Chinese AI firm MiniMax accessed by unidentified parties, researcher says
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers at Dragos said confidential links and other data submitted to Chinese AI firm MiniMax were accessed by unidentified parties, including after users requested that data not be retained. MiniMax said its systems automatically opened links to check for threats, deleted stored addresses and found no evidence chats or AI responses were disclosed. Atlas Cloud stopped forwarding requests and warned customers that secrets might be exposed.

articles.title: AirBaltic offers crew exit, demotion or Papua New Guinea secondment
articles.summary: Latvia's airBaltic has offered some staff voluntary exits, demotions or secondments to Papua New Guinea's Air Niugini as it restructures under Chapter 11, Reuters reported from employee emails and sources. The carrier plans to cut 500–700 jobs and reduce its Airbus A220 fleet. AirBaltic says options comply with labour law; a union disputes that and says it was not consulted.

articles.title: Malaysian air force facilities used to transport illicit drugs, minister says
articles.summary: Malaysia's interior minister said military aviation facilities were used in 21 transactions to move at least three metric tons of illicit drugs worth 156 million ringgit since August 2024. Seven air force personnel and six civilians were arrested as investigators pursue two criminal cells in Sabah. Authorities have not specified whether bases or aircraft were used; the inquiry is ongoing.

articles.title: India's top court tightens food warning labels in new setback for industry
articles.summary: India's Supreme Court ordered separate front-of-pack warnings for high salt, sugar and fat, tightening a government proposal that would have combined them in one label. The court's decision is a setback for the country's food and drinks industry and a win for health advocates seeking clearer consumer information. The food regulator must implement the specified hexagon warnings.

articles.title: Wife of Japanese journalist detained in Russia pleads for his release
articles.summary: Yuki Imai, a 34-year-old reporter for Hokkaido Shimbun, was detained in Russia's Sakhalin region in October on suspicion of espionage, his wife said in her first public comments. She appealed for his release, describing his two-year posting and young family. Japan has protested the arrest, which is straining already tense relations; Moscow has not publicly detailed the evidence.

articles.title: Insight: Prosecco's 'heroic' vines offer a test case in climate resilience
articles.summary: Growers in Italy's Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco region say the 2026 harvest held near last year's level despite record heat, drought and unusually warm nights. Reuters reports vineyards have adapted through less pruning, emergency irrigation and improved soil moisture, but these measures raise costs and may affect grape acidity. The experience offers a case study in climate adaptation, not proof the industry is insulated.

articles.title: Blake Corum runs for 184 yards as Rams dump Packers, extend win streak
articles.summary: Blake Corum rushed for a career-high 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams beat Green Bay 26–13 in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game. The Rams extended their winning streak to five, while Jordan Love threw two interceptions and the Packers lost a second straight. Green Bay receiver Christian Watson left with a concussion after a hit that led to a Rams safety's ejection.

articles.title: Indian farmers sell paddy stubble to biomass firms, reduce burning
articles.summary: Farmers in India's Punjab state are increasingly selling paddy straw to biomass plants instead of burning it, creating income and jobs while reducing a major source of seasonal air pollution. Farm fires fell 53% in 2025, but Delhi's air remained hazardous, showing the sector is still too small to change regional air quality. Analysts say procurement incentives and larger facilities are needed.

articles.title: Indonesian prosecutors name nickel firm and its owner as money laundering suspects
articles.summary: Indonesian prosecutors named nickel miner PT BSJ and its beneficial owner as suspects in an alleged money-laundering case tied to corruption in obtaining a mining permit from 2021 to 2026. Investigators say proceeds came partly from nickel ore sales under the licence. The owner could not be reached for comment, and the company did not respond to Reuters.

articles.title: Air cargo demand from AI data centres shows no sign of slowing, SATS CEO says
articles.summary: SATS, the world's largest air-cargo handler, says demand tied to AI data-centre projects remains strong, with server racks and semiconductors driving cargo growth despite volatility in technology shares. CEO Kerry Mok told Reuters the trend continued through the peak season, while SATS volumes have outpaced the global industry's growth rate for 12 consecutive quarters. The outlook depends on continued AI infrastructure investment.

articles.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, FT reports
articles.summary: Reuters reported, citing the Financial Times, that Nvidia told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The move follows new U.S. export-license requirements for advanced chips to several Southeast Asian countries, intended to block diversion to Chinese buyers. The report did not provide a detailed company statement explaining the halt.

articles.title: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN launch talks on digital payments across borders
articles.summary: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN agreed to form a working group on connecting domestic payment systems and coordinating rules for digital assets across borders. Finance and central-bank officials met in Kyoto and also discussed an emergency lending mechanism that took effect this month for shocks such as natural disasters and pandemics. The initiative reflects rising demand for faster regional digital transactions.

articles.title: Viettel, Singtel start building submarine cable linking Vietnam, Singapore and Thailand
articles.summary: Viettel and Singapore Telecommunications have begun building a 2,500-kilometre submarine cable linking Vietnam, Thailand and Singapore, with a planned capacity of 600 terabits per second and completion targeted for late 2030. The Vietnam-Singapore segment alone is designed for 240 Tbps. The project also involves VNPT, FPT Telecom and Thailand's AIS, expanding regional connectivity as demand for data grows.

articles.title: Airline Norse Atlantic suspends flights, warns of possible bankruptcy
articles.summary: Norse Atlantic suspended flights as high fuel costs and a worsening cash position left the long-haul budget carrier seeking urgent financing. The company warned it may file for bankruptcy if a short-term solution is not secured, while discussing a possible takeover with investors. The announcement follows an 85% share-price plunge and has already forced Pakistan International Airlines to shift affected UK routes to its own aircraft.

articles.title: Police use tear gas to disperse fresh Bangladesh garment worker protests
articles.summary: Bangladesh police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse garment workers blocking a major highway, a day after a panel approved a 36% minimum-wage increase that protesters say is inadequate. A police motorcycle was set on fire in Gazipur, a major manufacturing hub; authorities said the situation later calmed. The industry employs millions and supplies much of the country's export earnings, making wage disputes economically significant.

articles.title: Lukoil's global retreat driven by politics, co-founder says
articles.summary: Lukoil co-founder Vagit Alekperov said Western sanctions, rather than a voluntary business decision, drove the Russian oil major's planned withdrawal from overseas markets. He said the company still hopes to return internationally. The portfolio spans about 40 countries and produces roughly 350,000 barrels a day; Todd Boehly has signed a proposed deal with a U.S.-backed consortium to acquire the assets, subject to approvals.

articles.title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide orders
articles.summary: Myanmar's military-backed president said the government would reject International Court of Justice measures it considers inappropriate, days after the court found the military responsible for genocide against the Rohingya. The ICJ ordered investigations, prosecutions, guarantees against recurrence, support for displaced people and compensation; enforcement options are limited. More than 730,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh during the 2017 crackdown, and about 1.2 million now live in camps.

articles.title: Singapore 'very disappointed' over new tariffs, urges US to reconsider
articles.summary: Singapore's trade ministry rejected the U.S. Trade Representative's proposed maximum 20% tariff, which could fall to 10% if a reciprocal deal is reached, and said it would press Washington to reconsider. Officials argue the findings ignore Singapore's open, market-oriented economy and a U.S. trade surplus under their existing free-trade agreement. The dispute follows an eight-month U.S. investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity.

articles.title: German consumer sentiment edges up into December, survey finds
articles.summary: Germany's consumer-climate index rose 0.7 points to -30.2 heading into December, but remained well below a healthy level and slightly missed analysts' expectations. Income expectations improved modestly, while economic expectations fell and price expectations increased. Researchers said the weak reading points to cautious Christmas spending, underscoring how persistent uncertainty and cost pressures continue to restrain household demand.

articles.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza; Spain launches pollution plan
articles.summary: The Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre sank about 25 nautical miles off Ibiza while carrying as much as 7,000 metric tons of diesel. All 17 crew members were rescued, but one later died and six were treated for minor injuries. Spain activated its second-highest maritime pollution response and sent specialist vessels to survey waters important to sea turtles, dolphins and seagrass; the cause and any spill remain unknown.

articles.title: UK regulator finds errors in motor finance redress calculation amid legal battle
articles.summary: Britain's Financial Conduct Authority said errors in classifying a small group of loan agreements affected calculations for its £9.1 billion motor-finance compensation scheme. The estimated effect is less than one percentage point around the 17% adjustment, but the disclosure adds uncertainty as Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen and others challenge the scheme. The FCA asked Barclays to pause full-and-final settlement offers while it reviews the issue.

articles.title: Britain signs £8 billion deal to upgrade submarine facilities
articles.summary: Britain signed a five-year, £8 billion contract with Babcock to upgrade nuclear-submarine maintenance facilities, aiming to reduce delays that have kept Royal Navy vessels on longer deployments. Defence officials cite a growing Russian threat and say the nuclear deterrent is a priority despite tight public finances. The programme is expected to create about 3,000 skilled jobs and 2,500 apprenticeship and graduate roles.

articles.title: UK's Halfords raises lower end of annual profit forecast on warm weather and turnaround plan
articles.summary: Halfords raised the lower end of its fiscal 2027 underlying pretax-profit forecast to £60 million from £55 million, citing warmer-than-usual autumn weather and progress on a turnaround plan. The retailer reported first-half adjusted pretax profit up 66% to £39 million. Planned investments in marketing, technology and a national distribution centre are intended to improve efficiency, though the full benefits will take time to emerge.

articles.title: UniCredit seeks Commerzbank shareholder vote as it completes process to take control
articles.summary: UniCredit asked Commerzbank to convene a shareholder vote on appointing new representatives to its supervisory board after Poland's financial regulator granted the final authorization needed to receive shares secured through its takeover offer. UniCredit says its near-50% position should be completed through a share swap by December 7. The move advances a two-year contest between the Italian and German lenders, though integration and governance questions remain.

articles.title: Dollar rally takes a pause for Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The U.S. dollar paused near this year's highs as falling Treasury yields and a partial recovery in equities tempered demand for safe-haven assets ahead of Thanksgiving. Investors are weighing whether a slowdown in the AI trade could weaken U.S. growth and alter expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Thin holiday trading may amplify moves; the yen was near 159.19 per dollar and sterling slipped 0.2%.

articles.title: Vietnam seeks US trade deal as tariffs threaten clothing, footwear exports
articles.summary: Vietnam said it was working with Washington to complete a trade agreement after the Trump administration threatened tariffs of up to 35% on its exports, including clothing, footwear and electronics. Officials hope a deal could bring the rate closer to 20%, keeping Vietnam competitive with regional rivals. Manufacturers warn the uncertainty is already affecting orders and investment decisions; negotiations and a separate U.S. intellectual-property investigation remain unresolved.

articles.title: South Korea unification minister nominee pledges 'realistic' approach to North Korea
articles.summary: South Korea's nominee for unification minister, Hong Ihk-pyo, said he would pursue practical, lower-level steps to improve relations with North Korea rather than prioritize high-level talks. His nomination follows a cabinet reshuffle and disagreements within President Lee Jae Myung's government over engagement with Pyongyang. Hong said policy adjustments may be needed, but the two Koreas' strained ties and North Korea's resistance leave prospects for dialogue uncertain.

articles.title: US chip curbs, distillation crackdown threaten Chinese AI model development, sources say
articles.summary: U.S. chip-export rules and stronger safeguards against AI-model distillation may delay releases from Chinese developers Z.AI and Moonshot, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the firms. Z.AI's planned GLM-5.5 could slip into 2027, while Moonshot fears its release cycle could double if overseas computing access is cut. The rules target advanced U.S. chips in foreign data centres; the companies did not confirm the reported timelines.

articles.title: Portugal aims for 2027 surplus, PM refuses to enact deficit-driving tax cuts
articles.summary: Portugal's prime minister said he still expects a 2027 budget surplus after parliament-approved tax cuts pushed the official forecast to a 0.2% deficit. The measures, including a proposed temporary zero VAT rate on essential foods and capped fuel taxes, could cost about €800 million. Luis Montenegro said his government would not implement some provisions and may seek a Constitutional Court ruling, setting up a dispute over parliament's budget authority.

articles.title: What to know about Taiwan’s local elections and why they matter to China
articles.summary: Taiwan will elect mayors, council members and local officials across 22 cities and counties on Saturday, with the Democratic Progressive Party and Kuomintang competing in closely watched races. Campaigns have focused mainly on local services and issues such as solar panels on reservoirs, rather than cross-strait policy. China remains in the background: Taiwanese officials warn of increasingly sophisticated disinformation, while analysts say local results could shape party politics.

articles.title: A Chinese consumer advocate is stranded in South Korea as a crackdown in China targets campaigners
articles.summary: Chinese consumer-rights advocate Wang Hai is stranded in South Korea with his wife and two children after fleeing a crackdown on people accused of making 'malicious compensation claims.' Wang says staff were detained, his offices closed and his accounts frozen; South Korea rejected the family's asylum applications and the U.S. revoked his tourist visa. He has appealed and is seeking resettlement elsewhere, while Beijing says it is unaware of his case.

articles.title: India asks Netflix not to air Pakistani show, local media report
articles.summary: India's government has asked Netflix not to stream a Pakistani series in the country, Reuters reported, following a complaint from a film-workers' union. The series, Netflix's first Urdu-language production, is scheduled for global release on December 4. Officials cited an earlier commitment not to offer Pakistan-originated content in India; Netflix had not responded to Reuters, and the reported request's legal status remains unclear.

articles.title: Kenya cult leader found guilty of new assault and cruelty charges
articles.summary: Kenyan preacher Paul Mackenzie was found guilty of assault and cruelty to children in a new case linked to his Good News International Church. A court said six children were allegedly forced to fast and punished if they tried to eat or escape; 11 followers were charged and 24 people acquitted. Mackenzie, already serving 200 years for the deaths of 191 people, is due to be sentenced on the new charges December 17.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola cases surpass 12,000 as fighting disrupts response in east
articles.summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 12,000, government data cited by Al Jazeera show, as fighting in Ituri disrupts the response. About a dozen people, including two WHO personnel and Congolese health workers, were evacuated after being trapped in a hospital for three days. Clashes have displaced civilians and forced response teams from affected areas, complicating surveillance, treatment and containment.

articles.title: Gold drifts lower as Fed rate-hike fears loom
articles.summary: Spot gold was down 0.4% at $3,565.41 an ounce by 0830 GMT after briefly falling below $3,500 the previous day, its first move under that level since September 2025. Reuters attributed pressure to persistent U.S. inflation and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes. Higher rates make non-yielding bullion less attractive, though central-bank buying and future market shocks could support prices.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts wave of retaliatory Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and two drones over its Eastern Province, while a projectile caused minor damage at Jazan port without reported civilian injuries. The Houthis also claimed attacks on Jeddah and the Ras Tanura oil complex; the coalition said it intercepted four drones near the refinery. The competing claims leave the full extent of damage uncertain as attacks spread across ports and energy sites.

articles.title: Trump's new tariffs aim to prise global trade from China's grip
articles.summary: Washington's latest tariff plan is designed to pressure China by adding a proposed 20% duty to existing 25% first-term levies, Reuters reports. The proposal leaves room for tariffs to reach 40% if the current trade truce expires in January and uses measures on third countries to push partners to curb Chinese exports. The administration says the measures fit within the truce; implementation and scope remain subject to review.

articles.title: Hong Kong marks deadly fire anniversary with flowers, prayers and tears
articles.summary: Hong Kong residents marked the first anniversary of the Wang Fuk Court fire, which killed 168 people, with flowers, prayers and memorials. The government had urged caution about commemorations it said could be exploited for disruption; rights groups and some survivors criticized the warning as chilling public mourning. Survivors remain displaced or in temporary housing, while questions about responsibility and fire-safety reforms remain unresolved.

articles.title: Japan property investment hits record as global funds target Tokyo and Osaka
articles.summary: Commercial property investment in Japan reached a quarterly record of 2.21 trillion yen ($13.9 billion) in the third quarter, up 4% year over year, while overseas purchases rose 30%, Reuters reported. Investors are targeting Tokyo and Osaka offices, hotels, logistics and data centres as rents rise and vacancies tighten. Higher interest rates, yen volatility and development costs are making leveraged core assets less attractive, so advisers favour selective, value-adding deals.

articles.title: Investors turn bullish on Indian rupee as Southeast Asian currency bets sour
articles.summary: A Reuters poll found investors bullish on the Indian rupee for the first time in 18 months, supported by more than $14 billion in November foreign-equity inflows and lower oil prices. The rupee recently reached an eight-month high, while bearish bets increased on the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Philippine peso. Analysts caution the rupee's gains may be tactical as reserve rebuilding and a strong dollar could reverse the trend.

articles.title: Bank of Japan earnings fall as interest payments on reserves climb
articles.summary: Bank of Japan net income fell to 1.55 trillion yen in the first half of fiscal 2026 from 1.71 trillion a year earlier as higher rates increased payments on banks' excess reserves. The BOJ spent 1.91 trillion yen on reserve interest, exceeding income from government bonds, while ETF dividends partly offset the cost. The figures illustrate how policy normalisation is reshaping the central bank's balance sheet.

articles.title: China urges Japan to stay out of South China Sea disputes
articles.summary: China's defence ministry told Japan to stop commenting on South China Sea disputes, arguing Tokyo is not a party to them. The remarks followed Japan's plan to provide the Philippines with coastal-surveillance radars and drones. Beijing's claims overlap those of several Southeast Asian states; a 2016 international tribunal rejected the legal basis for China's expansive claims, a ruling Beijing continues to reject.

articles.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to meet on mutual defence pact
articles.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey will meet in Islamabad on November 27–28 to discuss their mutual-defence agreement, two Pakistani sources told Reuters. The Saudi and Turkish foreign ministers are expected to attend. The pact was signed in Mecca in August as regional tensions rose over the US-Israeli war with Iran. The meeting could deepen security coordination among three influential Muslim-majority states, but no new commitments were announced.

articles.title: Iraq court sentences eight French nationals to life for joining Islamic State
articles.summary: An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison for joining the Islamic State group, AFP reported. Two other French defendants received 15-year terms, while verdicts for 10 more were postponed. The cases follow transfers of foreign detainees from Syria to Iraq, where authorities have been processing people accused of joining the group. The convictions and remaining proceedings may carry diplomatic and human-rights implications.

articles.title: Israel kills nine Palestinians in Gaza strikes despite ceasefire, medics say
articles.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza overnight, medics told Reuters, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada and his wife. Separate strikes killed six people in Gaza City, and later gunfire killed a man in Bureij. Israel said Abu Nada managed Hamas financial networks; Hamas confirmed his death but did not address the allegation. The attacks continued despite the year-old ceasefire.

articles.title: FedEx airplane overruns runway at Miami airport, disrupting Thanksgiving travel
articles.summary: A FedEx MD-11 arriving from Memphis overran a runway at Miami International Airport around 8:40 p.m. Wednesday, temporarily closing all but one runway and causing hourslong delays into Thanksgiving morning. Authorities reported no injuries. The FAA is investigating, and FedEx said the aircraft experienced an issue on landing. The incident revived attention to runway safety after a separate fatal cargo-plane overrun at the airport in September.

articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
articles.summary: After a nearly 24-hour Exchange Online and Outlook outage disrupted millions of customers, Microsoft declared an internal “Code Red” and began daily engineering reviews. The Verge reports the trigger was a gateway-server bug present since July; response teams struggled across 11 Teams chats and a 1,000-person bridge call. Microsoft now targets recovery within an hour, but that goal has not yet been demonstrated.

articles.title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
articles.summary: 1Password said an intruder accessed an employee’s corporate GitHub account on Nov. 19, then used it to push malicious code into internal systems and download some customer data. TechCrunch reports names, sign-in email addresses, account identifiers and account activity dates were exposed; password vaults, passwords and secret keys were not accessed. The company has not disclosed how many users were affected or whether all were notified.

articles.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
articles.summary: WhatsApp began a global rollout of scheduled messages for individual and group chats on iOS and Android. Users can hold the send button and choose a delivery time from 10 minutes to 14 days later; text, photos and videos are supported, and messages send even if the phone is offline. TechCrunch says users can view or delete scheduled messages, but editing a schedule was unclear at launch.

articles.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
articles.summary: Google’s rejected “My Channel” patent describes a system that would generate personalized video feeds, advertisements and even full-length films using an AI model. The Verge reports it could draw on viewing history, age, IP address, GPS data and connected streaming accounts, and create avatars from users’ media. The filing is not a launched product; Google could appeal or resubmit an amended patent.

articles.title: First generic HIV drug shipments arrive in Africa, Global Fund says
articles.summary: Generic shipments of lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injectable used to prevent HIV, have arrived in Zambia, with deliveries to Uganda expected soon and Zimbabwe next year. Reuters reports more than 189,000 people in 10 countries had received a first dose by November, and 24 countries are expected to receive the drug by year-end. Generic supply is intended to ease shortages and expand access.

articles.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie settle years-long legal battle over joint French winery
articles.summary: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie settled their years-long dispute over Château Miraval, the French winery they co-owned, and both sides moved to dismiss their claims. The Guardian reports the settlement terms remain confidential. The litigation began after Jolie sold her stake in 2021; filings included allegations about Pitt’s conduct that he denied. The settlement ends the civil dispute without publicly resolving those allegations.

articles.title: Wall Street recovers most early losses as pullback in AI stocks eases
articles.summary: U.S. stocks closed mixed after a sharp intraday selloff in AI shares faded: the S&P 500 fell 0.3% after being down 3.2%, the Nasdaq lost 0.6%, and the Dow gained 0.3%. Nvidia finished down 3.9%. AP linked volatility to doubts about AI returns, 3.8% annual inflation, proposed tariffs and higher oil. Brent settled at $94.61; markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.

articles.title: Schumer, Van Hollen add to tallies of supporters for majority leader
articles.summary: Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen each gained a public endorsement as Senate Democrats prepare to choose their next leader by secret ballot. Mark Warner backed Schumer, who had 16 publicly declared supporters, while senator-elect Troy Jackson endorsed Van Hollen, who said about 15 Democrats supported him. More than two dozen remained publicly uncommitted; a candidate needs 28 votes if all eligible Democrats participate.

articles.title: Legal aid for DAPNs and DAPOs
articles.summary: England and Wales began national rollout of Domestic Abuse Protection Notices and Orders after a pilot that started in November 2024. The Legal Aid Agency clarified when civil and criminal legal aid can cover applications, breaches and appeals for victims and alleged perpetrators. A notice is a short-term police measure; an order is made by a court. The rules distinguish funding by case type and proceeding.

articles.title: Huge funding boost for communities leading the way in preparing for coastal erosion
articles.summary: England awarded more than £11.2 million to 12 council-led projects testing ways to prepare for coastal erosion, including drone surveys, cliff modelling, dune monitoring and highway adaptation. The Environment Agency estimates about 20,000 homes and businesses could face coastal change by 2105. The pilots will run until March 2029, with lessons shared nationally; some communities may need planned relocation rather than stronger defences.

articles.title: First national principles to help Australians with assistance animals
articles.source: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing
articles.summary: All Australian governments endorsed six national principles for regulating assistance animals, aiming to make accreditation and public access rules more consistent. The framework covers trainer standards, animal accreditation, public-access tests, evidence for handlers, a national identity card and animal welfare through retirement. The government says 95% of assistance-animal users report difficulties in public places; an implementation plan is still to come.

articles.title: Police super-complaint on the policing of image-based abuse
articles.summary: Three policing bodies in England and Wales accepted a super-complaint alleging systemic failures in how police handle image-based abuse, including the sharing of intimate images without consent. The complaint was submitted by the Centre for Women's Justice, Not Your Porn and law firm Leigh Day. Eligibility means it will be investigated; it is not a finding that individual officers or forces breached the law.

articles.title: UK cracks down on online abuse ahead of international summit seeking to end violence against women and girls
articles.summary: Britain launched a £27 million Thrive programme to counter online abuse of women and girls, including AI-assisted stalking, harassment and non-consensual intimate images. The government says it will work with technology companies on safer product design, such as automatic image blurring and age restrictions, and help other countries strengthen laws. A London summit on violence against women and girls is scheduled for April 27–28, 2027.

articles.title: Card payments edge past cash in shops; euro area consumers want both
articles.summary: Cards accounted for 45% of euro-area in-store payments in 2026, narrowly exceeding cash at 44% for the first time since comparable data began in 2016, the ECB said. Mobile payments reached 9%, up from 6% in 2024. Yet 62% of consumers still value cash access, 82% value digital options, and 19% of recent ATM users reported withdrawal difficulties.

articles.title: Regulators implement growth-friendly securitisation reforms
articles.summary: Britain's Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority issued revised securitisation rules intended to make funding and lending more efficient while preserving safeguards. Changes simplify disclosure and due diligence, allow more flexible ways to retain risk while keeping a 5% minimum, and permit limited simple re-securitisations. Regulators estimate £168 million in industry savings over ten years; some FCA rules still require finalisation.

articles.title: Government unveils shift towards public control of vital utilities
articles.summary: First Secretary Louise Haigh set out plans to restore public oversight of energy and water infrastructure, arguing fragmented regulation and high costs are holding back investment. Measures include scrapping a proposed gas-shipper levy, changing grid connections and tougher penalties for network delays; a Water Bill is due in 2027. The government says water bills could rise 36% between 2025 and 2030 without intervention.

articles.title: New Trump tariffs would likely increase sugar prices in the US
articles.summary: The administration proposed a $440-per-metric-ton duty on raw sugar imports outside the low-tariff quota, ostensibly aimed at Brazil but applying to other suppliers as well. Analysts estimate the combined tariff on out-of-quota sugar could reach 193%; U.S. March sugar futures jumped 14.65% to 45 cents a pound. Industry groups warn food makers and consumers will face higher costs.

articles.title: International Paper names insider Nicholls CEO of DS Smith spinoff
articles.summary: International Paper named longtime executive Timothy Nicholls to lead DS Smith, its planned spinoff combining the company's Europe, Middle East and Africa packaging operations with the $7.2 billion DS Smith acquisition. The standalone business is expected to list on the New York and London exchanges around December 7. The separation follows board approval earlier this week.

articles.title: Poland's Orlen dismisses CFO, deputy CEO, shares fall
articles.summary: Poland's state-controlled oil refiner Orlen dismissed its chief financial officer Slawomir Jedrzejczyk and deputy CEO Marek Balawejder, sending shares down as much as 4.8%. The company gave no reason, and the Ministry of State Assets declined to explain, saying the supervisory board made the decision. The departures add uncertainty around governance at one of Central Europe's largest energy groups.

articles.title: Tardy batter bowled out without facing a ball
articles.summary: Melbourne Renegades batter Deandra Dottin was timed out in Australia's Women's Big Bash League after failing to reach the crease within a new 75-second limit. Brisbane Heat bowler Sarah Glenn hit the unattended stumps before Dottin faced a delivery. Renegades captain Sophie Molineux said the team made the call too late, calling it an unusual lesson for future matches.

articles.title: Brazil announces new credit rules to curb household indebtedness
articles.summary: Brazil's central bank and monetary council announced safeguards to curb household debt. Lenders will be barred from increasing unsecured exposure to customers more than 90 days overdue, and card limits will be gradually reduced for some people who miss full payments on three or more bills in six months. Most measures take effect July 1, 2027, amid high borrowing costs.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.summary: Andy Taylor, the guitarist and songwriter who helped shape Duran Duran's early sound, died at 65 after metastatic prostate cancer, his family and bandmates announced. Diagnosed in 2018, he co-wrote major hits including 'Rio,' 'Hungry Like the Wolf' and 'Girls on Film.' Taylor joined the band in 1980, before its international breakthrough with the 1982 album 'Rio.'

articles.title: Biomimetic coacervate lubricant protects OA joints
articles.summary: Nature Reviews Rheumatology describes a biomimetic polyzwitterionic coacervate engineered to restore the lubricating layer that breaks down in osteoarthritis. The material binds cartilage, forms a stable low-friction coating and can deliver therapeutic compounds; experiments found it reduced friction more effectively than clinical hyaluronic acid. It remains experimental, with human safety and benefit unproven.

articles.title: Gut microbes can adapt to our ageing bodies
articles.summary: Nature reports a study of more than 10,000 people that found age-associated genetic changes in gut bacteria, including an adaptation that may help one abundant species resist oxidative stress. Researchers compared microbial variation with nearly 250 human traits and found few mutations associated with disease. The findings suggest microbes evolve within ageing bodies, but do not establish a clinical treatment.

articles.title: BBC lodges urgent appeal against Trump's $10bn defamation lawsuit
articles.summary: The BBC asked the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit to dismiss Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation suit over a Panorama documentary that edited two portions of his January 6 speech together. The broadcaster says the program aired only in Britain and was not accessed in Florida. It apologized for the edit but denies defamation; Trump's deposition was postponed until January.

articles.title: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court cancels a key power contract and many wonder what's next
articles.summary: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court voted 5–4 to cancel the government's contract with LUMA Energy, the private operator of power transmission and distribution. Officials have one year to arrange a successor while outages persist; Gov. Jenniffer González says operations will not return to the public utility. A federal control board warned that no clear transition plan or replacement company is in place.

articles.title: Judge halts order for Georgia's Fulton County to give 2020 election records to state election board
articles.summary: A Georgia judge paused an order requiring Fulton County to give the State Election Board a digital copy of 2020 ballots and related records seized by the FBI, after county officials appealed. The board has sought to reopen election allegations; multiple courts and officials found no fraud that changed the result. The records dispute remains on hold during the appeal.

articles.title: Judge declines to issue a long-term ban on taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads critics called propaganda
articles.summary: A federal judge declined to extend a temporary ban on taxpayer-funded advertisements promoting President Donald Trump, ruling the Democratic National Committee had not shown it was likely to prevail after the midterms. The suit challenges at least 11 spots partly funded by a $20 million Homeland Security contract. A separate New York judge ordered three ads removed; the administration calls them public-service messages.

articles.title: New York court upholds Mayor Mamdani's rent freeze
articles.summary: New York’s state Supreme Court upheld Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s rent freeze for rent-stabilized apartments, rejecting landlords’ claim that his appointees compromised the Rent Guidelines Board. The freeze covers about one million of the city’s 2.3 million rental units for leases renewing through Sept. 30, 2027. The landlords argued the process was biased; the judge said they had not shown it was arbitrary or unlawful.

articles.title: Trapped on the Tarmac: 3-Hour Flight Delays Spike Under Trump
articles.source: The New York Times (via GV Wire)
articles.summary: U.S. flights are on pace for their highest number of tarmac delays exceeding three hours since 2009, according to Bureau of Transportation Statistics data cited by The New York Times. The report says the Transportation Department has issued no airline consumer-protection fines in nearly two years, although officials say investigations continue. The delays remain relatively rare but can leave passengers confined aboard aircraft for hours.

articles.title: Study: Climate change driving increased summer thunderstorm activity, flash flood risk in New England
articles.summary: An analysis of 40 years of hourly observations from 80 New England airports found that summer rainfall is increasingly concentrated in shorter, heavier thunderstorms. Researchers reported that storms averaged nearly 40 minutes shorter in 2000–2020, while the most intense downpours made up a 25% larger share of thunderstorm rain. They warn aging drainage systems may face greater flash-flood pressure as the climate warms.

articles.title: UC San Diego Brain Organoids in Space Reveal New Clues to Alzheimer’s Disease
articles.summary: UC San Diego researchers sent Alzheimer’s-modeling brain organoids to the International Space Station for 40 days and found that spaceflight responses differed by genetic background. The models showed distinct changes in disease-related proteins and gene activity, while researchers identified altered stress-response pathways. The findings are preliminary and do not show that spaceflight causes Alzheimer’s, but may help refine laboratory models of the disease.

articles.title: Tiny Robots Deliver Treatments to the Brain
articles.summary: Caltech researchers developed light-activated nanorobots designed to cross the blood–brain barrier and deliver medication. In mouse models of glioblastoma, the system delivered about five times more drug to the brain than nonactivated controls, slowed tumor growth and prolonged survival, while reducing systemic toxicity. The work is experimental; it has not been tested as a treatment in people, and further safety and efficacy studies are needed.

articles.title: ASU scientists create a new way to assemble complex structures at the nanoscale
articles.summary: Arizona State University researchers demonstrated a programmable system in which designed DNA cubes spontaneously assemble into complex three-dimensional structures. The team used computational design to limit assembly errors and built increasingly intricate forms, pointing toward reconfigurable nanoscale devices and 3D circuits. The work is a materials-design proof of concept, not a functioning nanorobot or electronic chip, and practical applications remain developmental.

articles.title: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
articles.summary: An analysis of about 219,000 people followed for up to 30 years found that later-born generations entered older age with higher memory performance and experienced slower decline than earlier cohorts. The Nature Medicine briefing says the combined advantage could help explain falling dementia incidence over time. The finding reflects population trends, not a guarantee for individuals, and does not eliminate other dementia risk factors.

articles.title: EU nationals will pay higher tuition fees than UK students, Burnham indicates
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham indicated that EU students will not receive the same domestic tuition rate as British students under a proposed post-Brexit reset deal. Negotiations remain unresolved, with the EU seeking equal treatment and UK universities concerned about losing international-fee revenue. The dispute could complicate parts of the wider agreement, although Burnham said tuition talks were separate from the main package.

articles.title: Japan's data centre boom faces growing revolt from urban residents
articles.summary: Japan’s rapid data-centre expansion is drawing opposition from residents near Tokyo, who cite generator fumes, noise, heat and fuel-storage risks as facilities move close to homes. About 60% of the country’s data centres are in the metropolitan region. The government is preparing an action plan and local guidelines, while residents in several cities seek binding protections and one group has challenged a project’s zoning approval.

articles.title: Australia's Flight Centre probes data breach in third-party system
articles.summary: Australia’s Flight Centre Travel said it was investigating unusual activity in a third-party accommodation-booking system that may have exposed a significant number of customer records. Some leisure brands and independent agents used the system, but the company said flight bookings were not affected. The disclosure sent shares lower in early trading; the company had not yet confirmed how many customers or what data were accessed.

articles.title: Shein warns recovery will take time as e-commerce fees bite
articles.summary: Shein warned its European sales may not recover until the second half of 2027 after third-quarter European revenue fell 27.6% to $2.98 billion and group revenue declined 6% to $10.27 billion. New EU parcel charges and the end of duty-free import treatment have raised costs. The company cut marketing spending while investing in European warehouses and seeking faster growth in Latin America.

articles.title: South Korea unveils draft stablecoin rules, potential easing of ICO ban
articles.summary: South Korea’s financial regulator released draft rules that would let domestic banks issue stablecoins, digital tokens pegged to assets such as national currencies. The proposal could also reopen debate over the country’s nine-year ban on initial coin offerings. The legislation still needs parliamentary approval, and regulators are considering how fintech firms could participate. The scope, safeguards and implementation timetable remain unsettled.

articles.title: Retailers face rising AI cyberattack threat ahead of Black Friday, many uninsured
articles.summary: Retailers face heightened cyber risk heading into Black Friday as AI tools make attacks faster, Reuters reported. Insurer CFC’s data show ransomware claims against retail, leisure and hospitality businesses are 50% more frequent in November than the monthly average, while only 43% of small and midsize retailers carry cyber insurance. Seasonal sales, payment data and complex supply chains increase the potential cost of outages.

articles.title: Kremlin rejects ex-UK PM Johnson's call for a token Western force in Ukraine as unacceptable
articles.summary: The Kremlin rejected former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s proposal for even a small Western force in Ukraine, calling any foreign deployment unacceptable. Johnson argued a limited logistical presence far from the front would signal that Kyiv can choose its partners. Moscow has repeatedly warned such troops would be legitimate targets, while former president Dmitry Medvedev raised the risk of a Russia-NATO confrontation.

articles.title: Aramco, S-Oil inaugurate $7 billion petrochemicals complex in South Korea
articles.summary: Saudi Aramco and South Korea’s S-Oil inaugurated the $7 billion Shaheen petrochemical complex in Ulsan, Aramco’s largest investment in South Korea. The facility is expected to add about 3.2 million metric tons of annual petrochemical capacity, with commercial operations scheduled for 2027. It will use Aramco’s crude-to-chemicals technology and supply feedstock to nearby manufacturers, including industries serving electric-vehicle and semiconductor demand.

articles.title: New Miss Universe's Puerto Rican hometown celebrates her historic win
articles.summary: Jennifer Barreto's hometown of San Sebastián celebrated her Miss Universe 2026 win with a public viewing party and a jubilant motorcade. The 27-year-old became the pageant's first married mother to win and Puerto Rico's sixth titleholder, ending a 20-year wait for the island. The organization began allowing married women and mothers to compete in 2023, a change that continues to draw debate about pageant rules and ideals.

articles.title: Ukrainian drones attacked industrial facilities in Russia's Syzran, authorities say
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones struck industrial facilities in Russia’s Samara region, including the city of Syzran, while a separate strike killed one person in Samara, local authorities said. The region hosts major oil refineries, but Reuters could not verify social-media claims that two refineries were hit. Officials reported 145 drones downed and power outages; President Vladimir Putin had pledged retaliation for recent Ukrainian strikes.

articles.title: South Korea to unveil EV industry support measures as Chinese competition grows
articles.summary: South Korea plans to announce measures to strengthen its electric-vehicle industry as domestic automakers face growing competition from Chinese brands. The Finance Ministry told Reuters that a tax credit for EVs produced and sold in South Korea is under discussion, but no decision has been made. The government said the package would be presented Friday; Chinese-made vehicles accounted for 43.5% of new passenger EV registrations in the first nine months of 2026.

articles.title: Moldova keeps emergency energy measures in place despite opposition
articles.summary: Moldova’s pro-European government kept most emergency energy powers in place for another 30 days after a state of emergency expired. Officials said the measures helped stabilize gas, oil and electricity supplies, while water conditions had improved. Opposition parties demanded an accounting and criticized the policy. Moldova imports most of its energy and remains exposed to supply risks linked to regional tensions and Russia’s war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Deere forecasts 2027 profit below estimates as farm equipment recovery remains muted
articles.summary: Deere forecast fiscal 2027 net income of $4.50 billion to $5.25 billion, below analysts’ average estimate of $5.91 billion, as weak crop prices and high input costs restrain farm equipment purchases. The company reported quarterly revenue above expectations and said large-agriculture demand may be stabilizing in North America. It expects precision-agriculture sales to grow, while construction equipment benefits partly from AI data-center investment.

articles.title: US airlines face higher costs from proposed Embraer duty
articles.summary: A proposed 10% U.S. duty on finished Embraer aircraft from Brazil could raise costs for American airlines because there is no domestic alternative for the company’s regional jetliners, analysts and executives told Reuters. The tariff could begin as early as January, while carriers already face higher jet-fuel costs. The scope remains uncertain for aircraft completed in Florida from unfinished imports.

articles.title: Baseball's MLB sues players' union, seeks ruling that lockout is legal
articles.summary: Major League Baseball sued its players' union seeking a court declaration that an expected lockout beginning next week is legal, escalating talks over a new collective bargaining agreement. The central dispute is a proposed salary cap; MLB's latest offer would set a $258.2 million cap and $180.2 million floor in 2028. The union called the lawsuit frivolous and accused owners of avoiding good-faith bargaining.

articles.title: Mexico announces diplomatic protest after US denies extradition of former TV host
articles.summary: Mexico said it will send a diplomatic note protesting the United States' decision to deport former television host Inés Gómez Mont to Spain rather than extradite her to Mexico, where she faces allegations of tax fraud, money laundering and organized crime. President Claudia Sheinbaum cited reciprocity after Mexico transferred more than 90 suspects to U.S. custody. Spain has also received an extradition request; the allegations have not been adjudicated.

articles.title: UN tribunal says agency lacked evidence to dismiss Palestinian aid worker
articles.summary: A UN dispute tribunal ruled that UNRWA failed to provide evidence supporting its dismissal of Palestinian aid worker Abu Awad after Israeli allegations linked him to Hamas. It awarded him one year's pay and $5,000 in moral damages, while saying it could not determine the underlying allegations. The ruling raises questions about the agency's dismissal process; it does not resolve wider claims concerning other staff.

articles.title: Italian church report records 57 priests jailed for child sexual abuse
articles.summary: A report commissioned by the Italian Bishops' Conference documented 378 cases involving 356 alleged abusers and 385 victims between 2001 and 2021; 57 priests received final prison sentences. The authors cautioned that church archives cannot show the full scale of abuse. Victims' advocates called the figures incomplete and urged structural reforms and mandatory reporting, while the conference agreed to create a permanent observatory.

articles.title: Nigeria seizes $227 million of methamphetamine and arrests five Mexicans
articles.summary: Nigeria's anti-drug agency said it seized methamphetamine valued at $227 million in Enugu state and arrested five Mexican nationals. Officials said the operation recovered 1.5 metric tons of meth, 6.7 tons of precursor chemicals and industrial equipment. Authorities described it as one of the agency's largest hauls this year, amid concerns that Nigeria is becoming both a transit route and a production base for synthetic drugs.

articles.title: Ecuador says talks with US focused on reviewing joint security operations
articles.summary: Ecuador's interior minister said talks with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth focused on reviewing joint operations, setting next steps and identifying Ecuador's needs. His comments followed a report that Washington paused joint military activity while investigating a deadly operation by Ecuadorean forces. The minister called the discussions productive and said an action plan remains in place; the status of any pause was not independently clarified.

articles.title: Nigeria's Tinubu vows to bring peace to insurgency-hit region
articles.summary: President Bola Tinubu promised to restore security in Nigeria's insurgency-hit northeast as he campaigns for a second term in the January 16 election. Borno state remains a Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province stronghold, while kidnappings and attacks continue. A recent poll cited by Reuters found more than half of respondents disapproved of his performance; Tinubu also said more than 70 abducted schoolchildren remained captive.

articles.title: Second US judge blocks Trump's latest birthright citizenship order
articles.summary: A federal judge in Washington blocked President Donald Trump's August order narrowing birthright citizenship, ruling that Supreme Court precedent left no room for the new exceptions. The injunction covers children in the class action and bars several federal agencies from enforcing the order against them. A second judge has now blocked the policy; the administration called the ruling activist and may appeal.

articles.title: Russian forces hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles, mayor says
articles.summary: Russian forces struck two sites in Kyiv with ballistic missiles late Wednesday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Two buildings on the east side of the Dnipro River were hit, with one badly damaged; casualties were possible, but officials had not confirmed a toll in the initial report. The attack adds to pressure on the capital as Russia continues missile and drone strikes across Ukraine.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim urges wider tactical nuclear weapons deployment on facility tour, KCNA says
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for tactical nuclear weapons to be deployed across multiple domains and said nuclear-material production was expanding, KCNA reported after a facility tour. The agency did not identify the site; released images appeared to show enrichment centrifuges and warheads, according to analysts. Experts said Pyongyang may be signaling it will negotiate only as a recognized nuclear-armed state.

articles.title: Islamic State attack kills two Syrian security personnel in Hasaka
articles.summary: An Islamic State attack on a security headquarters in Hasaka, northeastern Syria, killed two internal security personnel and wounded five, Syrian state media reported. Authorities said four attackers died, two in clashes and two in suicide explosions. Islamic State has continued operating through clandestine cells despite losing its last Syrian territory in 2019, and has renewed attacks on security forces under President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

articles.title: Senegal parliament opposes president's decision to implement revised budget
articles.summary: Senegal's National Assembly voted 128–9 to condemn President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's decision to implement a revised 2026 budget by decree after lawmakers rejected it. The dispute with former prime minister Ousmane Sonko's party threatens a proposed $2.2 billion IMF support programme tied to debt restructuring. Lawmakers said the government had not provided adequate transparency on public finances; Faye said he was safeguarding state operations.

articles.title: Barrick International chief meets Mali prime minister after mining dispute
articles.summary: Barrick Mining's newly appointed international-division chief met Mali's prime minister for the first time since the company and the military-led government settled a dispute over the Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex a year ago. The meeting suggests warmer relations after conflict over taxes, profit-sharing and control, during which four local executives were imprisoned. Barrick said it would comply with Mali's new mining code; it did not immediately comment.

articles.title: OPEC blames EU for COP31 collapse as fossil-fuel dispute deepens
articles.summary: OPEC Secretary-General Haitham Al Ghais rejected claims that oil producers caused the collapse of COP31, saying the EU and others walked away from negotiations. Producers opposed language on moving away from fossil fuels and backed carbon-capture references, which some developing nations called costly and unproven. Reuters also reported negotiators' concerns about Saudi influence; EU officials had not responded to OPEC's criticism.

articles.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites a massive fire on a highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 31 people
articles.summary: A fuel-tanker crash on Cairo's Ring Road ignited a fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21, Egypt's Health Ministry said. The blaze in Giza's Warraq district charred more than two dozen vehicles; prosecutors ordered DNA testing to identify victims. Officials said the toll was preliminary, renewing scrutiny of road safety and enforcement.

articles.title: US FinCEN takes some systems offline after cyber incident, official says
articles.summary: FinCEN took some systems offline after unauthorized access affected a limited subset of its network, a Treasury official told Reuters. Treasury is working with the FBI, CISA and outside forensic examiners to determine the scope. Officials said there was no evidence that Bank Secrecy Act or beneficial-ownership databases were breached; reporting relief was provided to filers disrupted by the outage. The investigation remains ongoing.

articles.title: US famine monitor to halt reporting as funding shortfall hits staff, sources say
articles.summary: More than half of FEWS NET's field staff could receive termination notices by December 1, leaving the U.S.-funded hunger-monitoring network unable to publish its planned December food-security update, Reuters reported. The State Department had not confirmed fiscal-year funding. FEWS NET works in more than 30 countries, including famine-risk areas such as Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan and Somalia; the timing of any funding restart remains unclear.

articles.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
articles.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX's Starmind plan for up to one million orbital data-centre satellites, with deployment to begin by November 2033, 100,000 due by 2035 and half the maximum by 2038. The authorization does not guarantee the full constellation will be built. Scientists have raised concerns about heat removal, launch emissions, orbital debris, collisions and interference with astronomy.

articles.title: Fed policymakers at odds over causes of high inflation
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials remain divided over whether stubborn inflation reflects temporary supply shocks or stronger demand, Reuters reported ahead of the December policy meeting. Economists expected October headline PCE inflation of 3.8% and core inflation of 3.2%, while some policymakers warned AI investment and resilient spending could entrench price pressures. Markets were pricing in further rate increases, though falling oil prices complicate the outlook.

articles.title: Carthage resident Al Gore buys his hometown Tennessee newspaper
articles.summary: Former Vice President Al Gore agreed to buy the Carthage Courier, a 113-year-old weekly serving his Tennessee hometown and Smith County. The sale from the Lake family is expected to close in coming weeks; the price was not disclosed and all four employees are expected to remain. Gore, a former military and newspaper reporter, said he wants to preserve the paper as an independent local voice amid widespread newspaper closures.

articles.title: Lawsuits allege ICE brutalized U.S. citizens and prisoners at for-profit jail
articles.summary: Two people arrested during immigration raids in the Chicago area filed lawsuits alleging excessive force by federal agents; one plaintiff is a U.S. citizen who says agents rammed her car and restrained her after she identified herself. Separately, four former detainees allege sexual abuse, forced labor and retaliation at a Louisiana ICE facility. These are allegations in pending legal actions, not court findings.

articles.title: Israeli judges recommend prosecutors drop one bribery case against Netanyahu
articles.summary: Judges in Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial recommended dropping one bribery case and reconsidering another, saying a conviction in the main case appeared unlikely. The recommendation is not a ruling; Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said prosecutors would review the court's comments. Netanyahu denies wrongdoing. The cases concern alleged regulatory favors for favorable media coverage and a proposed deal with a newspaper publisher.

articles.title: Former Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest' being renovated after blaze
articles.summary: Workers are repairing Bavaria's Eagle's Nest, the former Nazi guest house, after an October fire destroyed its roof and remaining original furniture. A man suspected of starting the blaze is being held in a psychiatric facility while the investigation continues. The site once drew about 300,000 visitors annually. Critics say it should remain in ruins to deter neo-Nazi pilgrimages; operators argue preservation supports monitored remembrance.

articles.title: Israeli opposition advances October 7 attack probe opposed by Netanyahu
articles.summary: Israel's opposition-led parliament gave initial approval to a bill creating an independent commission to investigate security failures before Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack. The measure passed 65–50 but needs three more votes. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opposes an independent inquiry and favors a government-shaped process. The vote comes as rival Gadi Eisenkot tries to assemble a coalition after Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority.

articles.title: Suspected militants kill at least 30 in Nigeria's Niger state, residents say
articles.summary: Residents told Reuters that suspected militants killed at least 30 people and burned homes in villages in Nigeria's Niger state, describing the assault as retaliation for earlier killings of Fulani herders. A village head said gunmen occupied some communities and blocked recovery of bodies; Reuters could not independently verify a circulating video. The governor announced compensation for victims' families and urged dialogue.

articles.title: US holiday travel ramps up with long airport lines and bad weather
articles.summary: AAA expects 81.5 million Americans to travel at least 50 miles from Tuesday through Monday, while TSA plans to screen 17.6 million passengers. FlightAware recorded more than 3,700 U.S. delays and 60 cancellations Wednesday; some airport security waits topped an hour. A major East Coast storm threatens high winds, coastal flooding and flight disruptions through Friday, while winter weather and king tides affect other regions.

articles.title: Steelers release Rodgers after quarterback blasts head coach McCarthy
