articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released Aaron Rodgers after the quarterback said he would not return and accused coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep during meetings. Rodgers had been benched for Friday's game against Denver and previously said this could be his final NFL season. The team has not publicly substantiated his claims about the coach.

articles.title: Federal Reserve survey finds modest growth but persistent price pressures
articles.summary: The Fed's latest Beige Book found slight-to-moderate growth in eight districts and no change in four, while consumer spending was flat and firms reported persistent energy, transport, health-care, insurance and tariff costs. AI-related data-center investment remained strong. The report adds business-level context ahead of the December meeting; October PCE inflation was 3.8% year over year, with core inflation at 3.3%, Reuters reported.

articles.title: 2 men charged over break-in at Prince William and Princess Catherine's country home
articles.summary: Two Albanian men were charged after prosecutors said they climbed a drainpipe and broke into Anmer Hall, the Norfolk country home of Prince William and Catherine, stealing a clock and six pairs of cufflinks. Police arrested them nearby after a search involving dogs, drones and a helicopter; a third suspect remains at large. No royals were at the property, and the defendants were remanded pending another hearing.

articles.title: Iraq to hold national dialogue on constitutional dispute with Kurdish Regional Government
articles.summary: Iraq's four top state authorities agreed to hold a national dialogue on December 1 to address constitutional disputes between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Regional Government. Tensions centre on oil fields, border crossings and the distribution of federal powers. The initiative follows a court ruling backing federal authority and comes amid Kurdish objections to troop and border-control moves. Whether talks ease the standoff will depend on both sides' willingness to compromise.

articles.title: The Latest: All 5 tons of lead azide were successfully destroyed in Iowa detonation, Army says
articles.summary: The Army said it destroyed all five tons of degraded lead azide without secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. EPA monitors detected no airborne lead immediately after the blast or more than an hour later; the agency had collected over 1,200 baseline samples and plans further air, soil and water testing. Officials called the operation successful, but environmental effects on nearby farms and communities remain under assessment.

articles.title: Drone strikes kill 19 civilians in Sudan's Blue Nile state, rights group says
articles.summary: Emergency Lawyers said drone strikes in Damazin, Blue Nile state, killed 19 civilians, including six women. The group blamed the Rapid Support Forces; AP reported 15 wounded, while an earlier Reuters account cited 20, leaving the injury count unsettled. The attacks add pressure on a region receiving displaced families as Sudan's war continues.

articles.title: New York bans AI toys, including those using internet to talk to children
articles.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on internet-connected AI chatbot toys, including talking dolls, stuffed animals and robots. The Guardian reports that an NBC News test found a toy marketed to children as young as three generated violent and sexually explicit material. Attorney General Letitia James says the state will enforce the law; the measure is aimed at child safety and privacy.

articles.title: Seven-year-old held at Texas immigration center asks Trump to release her
articles.summary: Seven-year-old Charlotte Ortiz, held with her mother at the Dilley family immigration center in Texas, wrote President Donald Trump asking to return to school and see her father. Her 29 days in detention exceed a 20-day limit established by a 1985 court settlement. DHS says her mother has a final removal order; the family disputes the circumstances. The case adds scrutiny to family detention and conditions at Dilley.

articles.title: Yemen's army reports 654 operations against Houthi positions
articles.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognized army said government forces carried out 654 operations against Houthi positions, killing or wounding 109 fighters and commanders. The military described 21 airstrikes, 577 artillery attacks, 36 drone strikes and 20 rocket-artillery strikes across several fronts, but provided no independent evidence; the Houthis had not commented. The claims come amid renewed fighting and a worsening humanitarian crisis after the 2022 truce collapsed.

articles.title: Nearly 800 displaced from Sudan's Abu Zabad in one day, IOM says
articles.summary: The International Organization for Migration said at least 795 people fled Sudan’s Abu Zabad area in West Kordofan in one day as fighting between the army and Rapid Support Forces intensified. Displaced families moved into neighboring localities and states, following several larger waves earlier in November. The agency described conditions as tense and volatile; the conflict, which began in 2023, has displaced about 13 million people.

articles.title: German police in North Rhine-Westphalia to replace Palantir with Celonis
articles.summary: Police in Germany’s North Rhine-Westphalia state plan to replace Palantir’s data-analysis software with a system from Munich-based Celonis after a Europe-wide tender. The new program will run on police-owned infrastructure, giving authorities greater control over data and processes; the contract may last seven years. Palantir criticized the decision, while privacy officials have raised concerns about sensitive data access by US intelligence services.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay to lead BBC's Top Gear revival planned for 2028
articles.summary: The BBC named celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay as the lead presenter for Top Gear’s planned return in 2028, with co-hosts still to be announced. Filming is expected to begin in 2027. The motoring show has been off air since a 2022 crash seriously injured former presenter Andrew Flintoff. The revival follows a pause announced in 2023 after the accident, which halted production.

articles.title: Netanyahu's Likud challenges results at 120 Israeli polling stations
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party filed a court appeal seeking new voting at 120 Israeli polling stations, citing alleged irregularities involving voter-identification information, according to Israeli media. The reports said the filing did not allege widespread fraud or bribery. Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party accused Likud of trying to delegitimize the result. Eisenkot faces a Dec. 6 deadline to form a government.

articles.title: Austria's population projected to peak in mid-2040s before decline
articles.summary: Statistics Austria projects the country’s population will peak at 9.36 million in the mid-2040s before declining to 9.04 million by 2080, revising earlier forecasts that suggested it could exceed 10 million. Fertility is expected to fall to 1.3 births per woman, while the share of residents aged 65 and older may reach 30.1% by 2080. Immigration and employment patterns will shape the pace of aging.

articles.title: Poland plans no-fly zone along eastern border to bolster NATO flank
articles.summary: Poland plans a restricted airspace zone along its eastern border, potentially taking effect in late December or early January, Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk said. The zone would extend several to dozens of kilometers inland as Warsaw strengthens NATO’s eastern flank after Russian missiles fell in eastern Poland. Tomczyk said any decision to intercept threats over Ukraine would require agreement among NATO members.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine awaits US date for next round of peace talks
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv is waiting for Washington to schedule another round of US-mediated talks with Russia, which he wants to include European representatives. Previous discussions in Abu Dhabi produced agreement in principle to broaden participation, but Russian officials said no decision had been made. The next meeting’s timing and format remain uncertain as strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure continue.

articles.title: Malaysia studies AI wealth fund to distribute technology gains
articles.summary: Malaysia is studying an artificial-intelligence wealth fund that could distribute some economic gains to citizens, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said. He directed the communications and digital ministries to examine options, citing a proposal by US Senator Bernie Sanders. Anwar also said foreign AI investors face conditions on water infrastructure and skills training, reflecting concern that rapid automation and investment could widen inequality and disrupt jobs.

articles.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills Hamas security official, wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli strike on Gaza City's Shati refugee camp killed Hamas northern Gaza internal-security chief Mohammad Majid Abu al-Ouf, his wife and two teenage daughters, according to Gaza officials. AP reported four deaths and six wounded; Israel's military confirmed it targeted al-Ouf. The attack came amid a series of strikes reported during an already fragile ceasefire.

articles.title: ‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation
articles.summary: Meta employees told the Guardian that the company’s accelerated shift from human moderators to AI systems has left smaller review teams and increased the scale of mistaken removals. Staff described difficulties handling nuance and languages beyond English, while researchers documented a rise in account takedowns. Meta denied political bias and said newer systems make fewer errors on average; the company’s opaque moderation process makes independent assessment difficult.

articles.title: 'Russia wants more than Ukraine,' says Germany's Merz as he defends aid for Kyiv
articles.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz defended continued military aid to Ukraine and a planned rise in German defence spending, saying Russia’s ambitions extend beyond Ukraine and its actions threaten wider European security. He cited tensions around the Baltic, Poland and cyber infrastructure; Moscow denies seeking confrontation with NATO. The position faces domestic opposition as cost-of-living pressures grow, while Germany plans to lift defence spending above €200 billion by 2030.

articles.title: 53 incoming House Democrats plan to boycott Harvard orientation over graduate-worker strike
articles.summary: Fifty-three newly elected House Democrats told Harvard they will skip a December orientation program if graduate student workers remain on strike. The lawmakers said attending would mean crossing a picket line. The dispute centers on wages and workplace protections, with the graduate union seeking higher raises than Harvard has offered. The boycott adds political pressure to negotiations but does not directly resolve the labor dispute.

articles.title: A new way to measure tides could improve local flood forecasts
articles.summary: Researchers at the Technical University of Munich and Oxford used four decades of satellite shoreline images to estimate tidal height along beaches at 100-metre intervals. They found differences approaching one metre across New Zealand's South Taranaki Bight, finer variation than conventional gauges and broad satellite averages reveal. The method could improve local flood and storm-surge forecasts, especially where tide gauges are sparse, though it needs wider testing.

articles.title: African insurgents take war to the skies with off-the-shelf drones
articles.summary: Reuters documents how inexpensive first-person-view drones are reshaping conflicts across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger. Armed groups have used tactics refined in Ukraine to threaten military vehicles, aircraft and infrastructure, eroding governments’ former air advantage. The reporting also describes Ukrainian training links to Sahel separatists. The shift raises security risks for regional forces and facilities, though the balance of power varies by country.

articles.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
articles.summary: Colombian security forces rescued all hostages held for nearly a day at an Éxito supermarket in Cartagena after an attempted armored-truck robbery. The army said more than 50 people were seized; President Abelardo de la Espriella said one suspect was killed after refusing to surrender. The airport temporarily suspended operations but was reopening. The incident unfolded amid wider attacks by rebel groups on government targets.

articles.title: Amazon to launch Amazon Autos in UK in early 2027 in first expansion beyond US
articles.summary: Amazon says it will expand its car marketplace to the United Kingdom in early 2027, its first move beyond the United States. Hyundai will be an initial partner, listing new and used electric, hybrid and petrol models; dealer group Vertu will also participate. Customers will browse, compare prices and reserve vehicles online, but complete purchases at dealerships, which retain control over pricing.

articles.title: Amnesty urges war-crimes probe into Ethiopian shelling in Tigray
articles.summary: Amnesty International urged an independent investigation after verifying 14 civilian deaths in four Ethiopian artillery attacks on Alamata in September. It also alleged that Tigrayan forces placed fighters in residential areas and schools, claims the TPLF rejected; Ethiopian authorities had not responded. The report comes amid renewed clashes and military movements near the Eritrean border, raising fears that the fragile 2022 peace agreement could unravel.

articles.title: AP photo essay documents homelessness beneath Barcelona's prosperous landmarks
articles.summary: An Associated Press photo essay documents people sleeping rough beneath Barcelona’s grand civic and commercial buildings as Spain’s housing crisis becomes a central election issue. A local nonprofit estimated about 2,000 people slept on the city’s streets nightly in December 2025, 43% more than in 2023. New-lease rents rose 42% over a decade, while shelters face waiting lists and complex referral rules.

articles.title: AP review: Disney's animated film 'Hexed' offers a familiar coming-of-age witch story
articles.summary: Disney's animated film 'Hexed' follows a teenager who discovers magical powers and enters a hidden witch realm, where her grandmother rules as queen. The Associated Press review praises the voice performances of Hailee Steinfeld, Jodie Foster and Rashida Jones, along with the film's visuals, but finds the chosen-one plot familiar and its middle section slow. The review sees the mother-daughter relationship as the film's strongest element.

articles.title: Atlantic hurricane season ends unusually quiet under strong El Niño
articles.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is effectively over with 10 named storms and only one hurricane, Isaias, the quietest season since 1983 by accumulated cyclone energy, according to the Washington Post’s meteorological analysis. A strong El Niño helped suppress Atlantic storms while supporting unusually active Pacific conditions. Forecasters say next year’s outlook remains uncertain because ocean temperatures and the El Niño–La Niña transition could change.

articles.title: Australia and Solomon Islands sign security treaty barring foreign military bases
articles.summary: Australia and Solomon Islands signed a security treaty naming Australia the island nation's primary security partner and barring foreign military or security bases on Solomon Islands territory. The pact follows concern over a 2022 agreement with China; Prime Minister Matthew Wale would not confirm reports that the Chinese deal will not be renewed in 2027. Australia also pledged cooperation on infrastructure, education, renewable energy and sport, while Beijing said its Pacific partnerships are not driven by rivalry.

articles.title: Australia passes broad new online safety law targeting harmful platform content
articles.summary: Australia passed a Digital Duty of Care law requiring online platforms to take proactive steps against harmful content and features, with potential fines of up to 5% of global revenue. The rules take effect in a year and permit regulators to use anonymous accounts during investigations. Technology groups warn the law’s broad definitions could encourage excessive removals and raise privacy concerns.

articles.title: Australia's Labor government wins Greens support for trust and private-jet tax changes
articles.summary: Australia's Labor government secured Greens support for changes to discretionary trusts after agreeing to end a tax concession for private-jet fuel and exempt pensioners from proposed cuts to older Australians' private-health rebates. A minimum 30% tax rate on trust income is projected to raise A$4.5 billion in its first year from 2029–30. The agreement helps move several bills through the Senate, but opposition figures say the tax changes could burden small businesses.

articles.title: Australian inflation heats up in October, core hits two-year high
articles.summary: Australia’s monthly consumer-price index rose 0.5% in October, taking annual inflation to 4.9% from 4.3%, Reuters reports. Fuel costs jumped 6.3%, while trimmed-mean inflation reached 3.8%, its fastest pace since 2024. The figures are above the Reserve Bank’s 2%–3% target band and have reduced market confidence in near-term rate cuts, although weak labor-market conditions still shape expectations.

articles.title: Berlin landlord warns expropriation proposals could deter property investment
articles.summary: Commercial property group Aroundtown warned that Berlin proposals to expropriate landlords with more than 10,000 apartments could discourage investment beyond the city. The debate has returned after state elections strengthened the Left Party, which backs taking over large housing portfolios. Aroundtown says uncertainty may reduce financing and property transactions, while arguing Germany's housing shortage requires more construction. The company says converting some office space to homes could help add supply.

articles.title: BP transfers 3,000 finance operations employees to India's Wipro
articles.summary: BP has agreed to transfer 3,000 finance operations employees in India, Hungary and Malaysia to Indian technology-services company Wipro during 2027, subject to conditions. The deal reflects a broader shift by multinational companies to outsource internal support functions as they seek lower costs and more automation. BP will retain oversight of standards and data, while Wipro gains experienced staff and a long-term service relationship.

articles.title: Bulgaria intercepts migrant boat carrying 35 people, including children
articles.summary: Bulgarian authorities intercepted a boat carrying 35 migrants after it entered the country's Black Sea waters and came ashore near Sinemorets. Children were among those taken for medical care and warm clothing, regional officials told state news agency BTA. Bulgaria recorded about 7,000 attempted entries by land and sea in the first nine months of 2026, down from roughly 12,270 during the same period in 2025.

articles.title: Cambodia hosts Chinese military for largest Golden Dragon joint exercise yet
articles.summary: Cambodia and China began their eighth Golden Dragon joint military exercise, a 15-day drill AP describes as the largest since the series started in 2016. Activities include counterterrorism, humanitarian assistance, anti-piracy and disaster relief. The exercise comes as China helps fund the expanded Ream Naval Base, raising concerns about its strategic role; Cambodia denies granting Beijing a foreign military base.

articles.title: Cardamom advertisement sparks legal dispute between Bollywood actor and Indian regulator
articles.summary: Bollywood actor Ajay Devgn is challenging a Maharashtra food-safety order telling him to stop appearing in advertisements for a cardamom product linked to a brand also known for banned betel-nut mixtures. Regulators say such promotions can act as indirect advertising for restricted products; Devgn argues cardamom itself is legal. The court case could help define India's rules on surrogate advertising, an issue with implications for public-health policy and celebrity endorsements.

articles.title: Catalan separatist Carles Puigdemont says he will return to Spain in December
articles.summary: Former Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont says he will end nearly a decade in Belgium and return to Spain on December 12, after the Supreme Court applied a 2024 amnesty law to close his criminal case. He plans to present a renewed independence proposal five days later. His return could affect post-election coalition talks, although support for Catalan secession has weakened as voters focus more on immigration, crime and housing.

articles.title: CD Projekt RED says GTA VI launch has not materially hurt fourth-quarter business
articles.summary: Polish game maker CD Projekt RED says the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has not materially hurt its fourth-quarter business, despite a dip in console engagement. Its chief executive noted that GTA VI had not launched on PC, where many of the company’s players are based. Third-quarter net profit fell 43%, leaving a demanding fourth-quarter target for its multi-year profit goal.

articles.title: China investigates Shanghai party chief in widening anti-graft campaign
articles.summary: China’s anti-corruption watchdog opened an investigation into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a member of the ruling Communist Party’s Politburo. Reuters says he is the fourth Politburo member targeted since 2025, following removals involving senior military and provincial officials. Authorities gave no details about Chen’s case; the probe nevertheless signals that Xi Jinping’s campaign continues to reach the party’s highest ranks.

articles.title: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer
articles.summary: A British lawyer who handles Interpol red-notice cases says China is using the system to pursue dissidents through criminal allegations that may conceal political motives. He cited five cases and raised questions about notices sought against UK-based Chinese activists ahead of Hong Kong hosting Interpol’s general assembly. Interpol said it was reviewing his inquiry but shared no substantive information. The claims are allegations; China and Interpol had been approached for comment.

articles.title: China urges Netherlands to provide certainty for firms amid Nexperia dispute
articles.summary: China's foreign minister urged the Netherlands to provide a predictable business climate for Chinese companies during talks with Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen. The appeal comes amid a continuing legal dispute over Nexperia, the Dutch-based chipmaker owned by China's Wingtech, after Dutch authorities intervened over national-security concerns. Both governments said they would keep communication open on semiconductors, but the company's control and governance remain contested.

articles.title: China-linked battery projects could receive UK funding despite security warnings
articles.summary: Ofgem's provisional shortlist for a UK long-duration storage subsidy scheme includes 11 lithium-ion projects, many reliant on batteries and software from Chinese suppliers. The Guardian reports that security specialists and industry sources worry the regulator's cost-focused assessment may underweight cyber risks over facilities' lifetimes. Ofgem says it is reviewing consultation responses; final funding decisions are expected in coming weeks. The debate pits cheaper storage against supply-chain resilience and domestic technology.

articles.title: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying 2 Chinese and 1 Pakistani astronaut
articles.summary: China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carried two Chinese astronauts and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to the Tiangong space station, marking the first foreign crew member on a Chinese crewed mission. The craft docked successfully and the new arrivals joined three astronauts already aboard. The mission includes more than 90 experiments and reflects growing China-Pakistan space cooperation; Pakistan hopes the flight opens the door to further joint missions.

articles.title: Citigroup weighs return to Venezuela after five-year absence
articles.summary: Citigroup is considering restoring banking services in Venezuela, five years after leaving the country, Bloomberg reported. Reuters says executives have discussed possible arrangements and sanctions waivers with U.S. State and Treasury officials; a first step could be correspondent banking rather than branches. Citi declined to comment. Any return would face a country still recovering from prolonged economic crisis and financial isolation.

articles.title: Cognizant in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ operations
articles.summary: Cognizant is in talks to take over parts of S&P Global’s Capital IQ operations, potentially transferring about 1,500 employees in India, Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the discussions. The terms remain unsettled and talks could fail. The move comes as S&P explores strategic options for its data businesses and companies increasingly outsource operations to reduce costs and reshape units for AI-era services.

articles.title: Container of Christmas decorations washes ashore in Bulgaria
articles.summary: Bulgarian authorities opened a shipping container that washed ashore near Burgas and found more than 80 boxes of Christmas decorations, including life-sized Santa figures and a polar bear. The cargo, valued at about €50,000, reportedly belongs to a Romanian company and may have come from a Greek vessel hit by drones in the Black Sea last month. The ship operator has not confirmed the container’s origin.

articles.title: Democrats clinch historic House majority of at least 259 seats
articles.summary: Democrat Victoria Broderick’s narrow Tennessee victory gave House Democrats at least 259 seats, their largest majority since 1992. AP said she defeated Republican Scott DesJarlais by fewer than 400 votes, a 0.18-point margin. One House race remained too close to call, while two Louisiana contests were headed to December runoffs. The result expands Democrats’ leverage when the new Congress convenes in January.

articles.title: Dolphins with active social lives and big friendship groups live longer, researchers find
articles.summary: A study in PLOS Biology used nearly 40 years of observations from Shark Bay, Western Australia, to link stronger, more stable social groups with longer lives among Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins. Researchers say group ties can help animals share information, find mates and maintain alliances, while also carrying risks such as disease transmission and stress. The findings show individual social preferences change with age; they do not establish that social contact alone causes longevity.

articles.title: EasyJet annual profit plunges 89% as fuel costs surge
articles.summary: EasyJet reported full-year pretax profit of £71 million, down 89% from the previous year, as fuel costs rose 11% to £2.5 billion despite a strong summer travel season. Reuters says the result missed analyst expectations and comes as Apollo’s £5.7 billion takeover proceeds toward a planned 2027 completion. The airline withheld next-year guidance because of the pending deal.

articles.title: English coastal communities receive £11 million for erosion planning and monitoring
articles.summary: Britain will distribute more than £11 million across 12 council-led projects to help English coastal communities monitor erosion and plan for rising seas. Measures include laser-equipped drone surveys, dune restoration, 3D modelling and moving roads inland. The Environment Agency estimates 3,500 properties could be at risk by 2055 and over 10,000 by 2105. The funding is intended to support earlier planning; it cannot prevent all shoreline retreat or protect every property.

articles.title: EU postpones discussion to approve Tesla's self-driving tech
articles.summary: The European Union postponed a committee meeting that could consider bloc-wide approval of Tesla’s assisted-driving system from December 1 to December 15. A vote may occur then, but approval would require support from 15 member states representing 65% of the EU population. The delay follows two earlier meetings without a vote after the Netherlands granted preliminary approval in April.

articles.title: Europe plans €50 billion sovereign tech equity fund to boost quantum technology
articles.summary: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act with a targeted €50 billion equity fund to help European companies scale quantum computing, secure communications and sensing technologies. The draft would favor EU suppliers in some public procurement while allowing bids from certain partner countries. EU governments and the European Parliament must still negotiate the law. The proposal aims to narrow a funding gap with the United States and China.

articles.title: Eurostar cancels trains linking London, Paris and Brussels after staff strike
articles.summary: Eurostar cancelled at least six services linking Brussels, Paris and London after staff began an unannounced strike, the company said. The operator did not specify how long the stoppage would last or provide further details to Reuters. The cancellations add uncertainty for cross-Channel travellers during a busy holiday period; passengers should check directly with Eurostar because the scale and duration of disruption were still unclear at publication.

articles.title: Ex-England soccer player Sterling spared immediate jail sentence for dangerous driving
articles.summary: Former England winger Raheem Sterling received a 12-month prison sentence suspended for 18 months after admitting dangerous driving while inhaling nitrous oxide before crashing his Lamborghini. A court also ordered 100 hours of unpaid work and a two-year driving ban. No one was injured. The judge cited the danger to other road users, while noting Sterling had engaged with addiction services after the incident.

articles.title: Federal judge permanently blocks sanctions against groups that share ICC evidence
articles.summary: A federal judge made permanent an injunction blocking the Trump administration from penalizing two organizations for sharing evidence with the International Criminal Court and Palestinian rights groups. The groups challenged an executive order threatening civil fines and criminal penalties for such cooperation. The court ruled that the order imposed an unconstitutional, content-based restriction on speech, limiting enforcement against the plaintiffs.

articles.title: German economy grows just 0.1% in third quarter after downward revision
articles.summary: Germany’s economy expanded just 0.1% in the third quarter of 2026, below an earlier 0.2% estimate, the federal statistics office said. Reuters attributes the revision to weaker exports and September retail activity. Investment fell 1.2% from the prior quarter, while household consumption rose only 0.1%, reinforcing signs that growth slowed after stronger first-half performance.

articles.title: Glee actor Jenna Ushkowitz says Cory Monteith tribute episode came too soon
articles.summary: Jenna Ushkowitz, who played Tina on 'Glee,' says the 2013 episode honoring co-star Cory Monteith aired too soon after his death. She told Variety that cast and crew were grieving privately while also acting out their characters' grief, and felt they lacked the support to handle both. Ushkowitz understood why fans wanted a tribute, but said the experience was painful. Monteith died in 2013 from an accidental overdose.

articles.title: Global airports court private capital to fund upgrades, raising cost concerns
articles.summary: Airport operators are turning again to private investors to help fund aging terminals, control towers and capacity expansions. Reuters says industry estimates point to more than $4 trillion in global airport infrastructure needs over three decades as passenger traffic could double by 2050. Officials warn private financing can raise costs, leaving governments to balance capital needs against user fees and affordability.

articles.title: Global temperatures stayed more than 2°C above preindustrial levels for six straight days
articles.summary: Global daily temperatures exceeded 2°C above preindustrial levels for six consecutive days for the first time, reaching 2.24°C above baseline on Monday, according to data reviewed by The Guardian. Scientists stress that a short daily streak does not mean the Paris Agreement's long-term threshold has been breached. They link the spike to human-caused warming and a strong El Niño, warning that drought and forest fires can amplify carbon buildup.

articles.title: GSK reports twice-yearly asthma drug matched Nucala in late-stage immune-disorder study
articles.summary: GSK said its twice-yearly medicine depemokimab performed comparably to its monthly drug Nucala in a late-stage study for the rare immune disorder EGPA. The company reported similar safety and efficacy, but detailed results have not yet been published. GSK plans to seek regulatory approval in the first half of 2027; the findings do not yet make the drug an approved EGPA treatment.

articles.title: Gulf stock markets mixed as traders assess Saudi tensions and US inflation
articles.summary: Gulf stock markets were mixed as investors assessed Saudi-Houthi escalation and awaited U.S. inflation data that could influence Federal Reserve policy. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark slipped 0.3%, while Dubai and Abu Dhabi edged higher; Qatar fell. Saudi Arabia also approved a 2027 budget projecting a 190-billion-riyal deficit. The figures are an early trading snapshot, not a full-day market result.

articles.title: Hollywood stars defend Iranian director Jafar Panahi after Tehran court sentences him in absentia
articles.summary: Nearly 2,000 actors, directors, festivals and film institutions had signed a statement backing Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi, according to Democracy Now. Panahi was sentenced in absentia by a Tehran court to five years and one month in prison. The Cannes Film Festival issued a separate protest, urging authorities to lift restrictions that prevent him from traveling, creating and expressing himself freely.

articles.title: Homeland Security secretary faces White House criticism over outage response
articles.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin faces criticism inside the White House over his handling of major technology outages and public appearances during the disruption. Officials say he was removed from television briefings after struggling to explain flight, banking and corporate-system failures. President Trump publicly backed him, while lawmakers seek answers about the outages and the department’s broader management and immigration enforcement.

articles.title: Hong Kong wildlife groups seek tighter exotic-pet rules after millions of imports
articles.summary: Conservation groups say Hong Kong imported 3.7 million live exotic animals from 86 countries and jurisdictions between 2020 and 2025, roughly 80 each hour. They are urging authorities to create an approved-species list and update rules that currently exclude some amphibians and invertebrates. Researchers warn poorly regulated trade can spread pathogens and parasites to people and native wildlife. Hong Kong's agriculture department had not responded to Reuters by publication.

articles.title: In landmine-ravaged Myanmar, a rebel with an artificial leg vows to fight on
articles.summary: Myanmar recorded 1,891 landmine and unexploded-ordnance casualties in 2025, the highest national toll for a third straight year, according to Landmine Monitor. Reuters followed a rebel commander who lost a lower leg and received a prosthetic near the Thai border, where a small workshop has fitted 150 people wounded in the conflict. Mines laid by both military and resistance forces contaminate nearly two-thirds of the country, putting civilians at continuing risk.

articles.title: India approves $1.2 billion incentive plan for construction equipment
articles.summary: India approved an eight-year, $1.2 billion incentive programme to expand domestic production of advanced construction equipment and reduce reliance on imports, particularly from China. The plan offers sales-linked support to manufacturers and component suppliers, plus grants for testing. It gained urgency after Chinese export controls on tunnel-boring machines took effect November 18. Officials estimate the programme could attract $2.27 billion in investment and replace some imports.

articles.title: India's central bank buys dollars for a fourth straight month
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India was a net buyer of foreign currency for a fourth consecutive month in September, purchasing $6.94 billion net, according to its monthly bulletin. Gross purchases reached $82.18 billion and sales $75.25 billion. The bank's forward dollar sales also increased. The data reflect efforts to manage currency flows, although the rupee later strengthened in November as oil prices eased and investors shifted toward Indian equities.

articles.title: Iran says it can withstand US naval blockade as inflation pressures mount
articles.summary: Iran’s first vice president said Tehran can withstand the U.S. naval blockade because more cargo is entering through land borders, while the government seeks to contain basic-goods prices. October consumer prices were 88.7% higher than a year earlier and food and beverage prices rose 112.6%, according to Iran’s statistics agency. Officials offered no quantified supply assurances, leaving the effect of the blockade uncertain.

articles.title: Japan's key services inflation gauge hits 36-year high
articles.summary: Japan’s services producer-price index rose 4.2% year over year in October, the fastest pace since 1990, according to Bank of Japan data cited by Reuters. Higher ocean freight, leasing and hotel costs drove the increase. The measure helps show whether companies are passing labor expenses to customers, strengthening the case for a possible near-term central-bank rate increase.

articles.title: Vance says Jensen Huang won't need a pardon as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal builds in Washington
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance said Jensen Huang is not under investigation and does not need a pardon, while Trump had called a pardon an option. Huang is scheduled for closed-door House interviews Dec. 1 and a public Senate hearing Dec. 3. S&P separately placed Nvidia on negative credit watch over unresolved board oversight and governance risks.

articles.title: Jordan court sentences man to death over attack that killed security officer
articles.summary: Jordan’s State Security Court sentenced a man to death for an attack that killed a security officer near the Sri Lankan Embassy in Amman on November 5. The court convicted him of terrorist acts resulting in death and weapons offenses, according to the armed forces. The ruling remains subject to appeal and automatic review, so it is not yet a final sentence.

articles.title: Kilmar Ábrego García hopes to return to US after Trump
articles.summary: Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Ábrego García arrived in Spain after a judge cleared his departure from the United States, where he had been wrongly deported in 2025 and later fought another removal attempt. His lawyer calls the move temporary and says he hopes to return to his U.S.-citizen wife and child after the Trump administration. Federal officials say he will not be allowed back; a separate criminal appeal remains pending.

articles.title: Kiwi return to Wellington hills after 150 years in Māori-led conservation milestone
articles.summary: A Māori-led conservation partnership has returned more than 250 wild kiwi to the hills around Wellington, where the birds had been absent for over 150 years. The Capital Kiwi project used more than 5,300 predator traps across 24,000 hectares to reduce stoat threats; its founder estimates the local population now exceeds 300, including wild-hatched chicks. Project leaders report chick survival above 90% in managed areas, though long-term success depends on sustained predator control.

articles.title: Labour remains committed to ban on conversion practices despite calls to scrap bill
articles.summary: Britain’s Labour government says it remains committed to a proposed ban on conversion practices in England and Wales, despite calls to amend or abandon the bill over free-speech, parenting and religious-freedom concerns. Equalities minister Bridget Phillipson said the measure targets abuse intended to change sexual orientation or gender identity and would not affect normal parenting. Details remain contested as the draft is debated.

articles.title: Latest review of Met police culture finds little has changed since last one
articles.summary: An independent review found institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia remain in London’s Metropolitan Police three years after the Casey report. It cited defensive leadership, weak organisational learning and staff fear of retaliation: only 44% felt confident raising concerns about a senior officer, while 17% had no confidence. The Met points to misconduct and vetting reforms, but the review warned further scandals remain likely without deeper cultural change.

articles.title: Lebanon prepares to reopen a second international airport in its north
articles.summary: Lebanon plans to reopen Kleiat Airport in the north as an international gateway from mid-December, with initial routes expected to serve Turkey, Egypt and Jordan. Private investors are expected to contribute up to $6 million, while the government upgrades roads. The project could bring jobs and travel links to the impoverished Akkar region. Its progress also reflects Hezbollah's reduced political influence after recent wars and shifts in Lebanon's power balance.

articles.title: Italy rebukes Ukraine over attacks on Russian ships in Libya
articles.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died from wounds suffered in Ukraine's drone strike on a Russian warship docked at Benghazi, the eastern Libyan National Army said. Ukraine said it deployed seven sea drones; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the vessel as a military target. Italy's foreign minister rebuked Kyiv, warning the operation violated Libyan sovereignty and risked widening the conflict.

articles.title: London Metal Exchange tightens aluminium trading rules after supply squeeze
articles.summary: The London Metal Exchange temporarily tightened short-term aluminium trading rules after falling inventories and concentrated holdings drove immediate-delivery premiums to their highest level since 1988. The changes require large holders of stock warrants and short-term futures to make metal available at capped prices. Available exchange inventories have more than halved this year. The LME says it will keep monitoring the market and may take further action if the squeeze persists.

articles.title: Powerful storm threatens East Coast with damaging winds, power outages, coastal flooding
articles.summary: More than 80 million people from Georgia to Massachusetts were under wind alerts as a powerful East Coast storm threatened damaging gusts, heavy rain and coastal flooding. New York and New Jersey declared emergencies, and organizers moved the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET. The delay reflects safety concerns for spectators and large balloons as king tides amplify coastal-water risks.

articles.title: Major fragrance suppliers fined £85 million by the CMA for illegal collusion
articles.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority fined Firmenich, Givaudan and International Flavors & Fragrances a combined £85 million after finding they shared sensitive information on pricing and commercial negotiations. The regulator said some firms coordinated price increases and agreed not to hire staff assigned to a major customer. The companies admitted breaking competition law; the fragrances are used in household cleaners, detergents, perfumes and colognes.

articles.title: Malawi hospitals face worst essential-medicine shortages in more than a decade
articles.summary: Essential-medicine availability in Malawi has fallen from 77% in early 2025 to 40% nationwide and as low as 18% at major referral hospitals, according to internal government supply data. Patients are being asked to buy basic items privately, even in public hospitals. The crisis is tied to foreign-exchange shortages and about $18 million in supplier arrears; officials say they have begun clearing debts to restore deliveries.

articles.title: Meta executives meet India's opposition amid protests over content moderation
articles.summary: Meta executives met India’s opposition Congress party as protests intensified over content removals and allegations that the company favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP, which Meta denies. Reuters reported Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts under Indian law in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025. The company made no commitments at the meeting and cited local legal requirements.

articles.title: Migrant arrivals in Spain's Canary Islands break single-day record
articles.summary: More than 2,100 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands in a 24-hour period, a new single-day record, according to maritime rescue data. One person was found dead and another gave birth during the crossing from West Africa. Most boats reached El Hierro, a key entry point. The arrivals intensified pressure on Spain's migration debate ahead of an election, while officials called for stronger regional cooperation and legal routes.

articles.title: Millions of UK households face 26% energy price-cap increase in January
articles.summary: Britain’s Ofgem raised the household energy price cap by 26% for January–March, taking the annualized bill for a typical dual-fuel household to £2,166. Reuters says the increase will affect about 20 million homes on variable tariffs and reflects higher wholesale gas prices linked to the Middle East conflict. The jump is likely to add pressure to household budgets and inflation.

articles.title: More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died during Ukraine war, leaked data suggests
articles.summary: Leaked Russian government records analyzed by BBC News and Mediazona suggest at least 490,334 Russian soldiers had died since the full-scale invasion began in 2022; another analysis of the dataset puts the toll closer to 700,000. The records reportedly contain more than 11 million entries through September 2026. The Kremlin has not released official totals and says only its Defense Ministry can publish them.

articles.title: Nationwide Greek strike disrupts ferries, metro and some flights
articles.summary: Greek public-sector workers and several private unions staged a nationwide strike demanding higher wages, restored annual bonuses and stronger health and education services. Ferry routes stopped, some metro services were cut and flights at regional airports were suspended as transport and telecommunications workers joined the action. The strike is the third in recent weeks amid pressure from rents and living costs; the government points to €2.2 billion in tax breaks and aid this year.

articles.title: Native American group wins partial ruling over Plymouth's National Day of Mourning protest
articles.summary: A Massachusetts judge ruled that Plymouth must honor a 1998 agreement allowing the United American Indians of New England to hold its National Day of Mourning protest without permits or insurance. The town no longer has to provide a mobile stage, however, and the ruling leaves room for future legal disputes. The group says the event will proceed, challenging efforts it views as limiting Indigenous speech and visibility.

articles.title: Netherlands pushes back against proposed US chip-export control bill
articles.summary: The Netherlands is lobbying against the proposed U.S. MATCH Act, which would pressure allies including the Netherlands and Japan to tighten export controls on chipmaking equipment sold to China or face unilateral U.S. restrictions. Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said Dutch export-control decisions should remain independent. ASML expects China to account for about one-fifth of its 2026 sales, making the dispute commercially significant.

articles.title: Nine more Ukrainian children reunited with families through US-backed effort
articles.summary: Nine Ukrainian children have been reunited with relatives, bringing the total to 43 under an initiative involving US first lady Melania Trump, the White House and Russian officials. The children were moved from Russia and Russian-held parts of Ukraine to relatives in Ukraine and Germany. Moscow says cooperation was secured with both sides, while Ukrainian authorities had not immediately commented. The cases remain sensitive amid international allegations about the wartime transfer of children.

articles.title: North Korea orders Swiss diplomat out and demands closure of Pyongyang office
articles.summary: North Korea ordered the head of Switzerland's newly reopened diplomatic office to leave within 48 hours and demanded the office close, calling Swiss sanctions on a children's camp hostile. Switzerland says the camp was involved in transferring Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied areas and promoting pro-Russia messaging. Pyongyang rejects the sanctions and says the camp is legitimate. Switzerland says it will keep diplomatic channels open despite the dispute.

articles.title: Oat sales rise as shoppers seek filling foods amid GLP-1 popularity
articles.summary: Waitrose says sales of its Scottish oats rose 124% this year as shoppers seek filling, fibre-rich foods amid the popularity of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. A retailer survey found 64% of respondents were actively choosing foods that help them feel full for longer, while many GLP-1 users reported changing household shopping. The Guardian notes that social-media labels such as 'nature's Ozempic' are marketing shorthand: oats are not equivalent to prescription medication.

articles.title: Paralympian Ezra Frech becomes first Paralympian to win Dancing with the Stars
articles.summary: Paralympic track-and-field gold medalist Ezra Frech won the U.S. edition of Dancing with the Stars, becoming the show's first Paralympian champion and youngest male winner. The 21-year-old and professional partner Daniella Karagach beat Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and four other finalists. Their freestyle included a prosthetic-leg mishap, but Frech recovered and finished the routine; judges' scores and viewer votes determined the result.

articles.title: Peppermint oil linked to lower blood pressure in small 20-day trial
articles.summary: A randomized study of 40 adults with elevated blood pressure or stage 1 hypertension found that participants taking food-grade peppermint oil had an average systolic reduction of about 8.5 mmHg versus placebo after 20 days. The University of Lancashire team published the findings in PLOS One. The trial was small and brief, so larger studies are needed; it does not justify replacing prescribed treatment.

articles.title: Plane crash off the coast of Mississippi kills 6, including 2 children
articles.summary: A Cessna 210 traveling from New Orleans to Fort Myers crashed in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula and Horn Island, killing all six aboard, including two boys ages 8 and 10, the Coast Guard said. Divers recovered the victims from the fuselage after a lengthy search. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate; officials have not announced a cause.

articles.title: Pope creates Vatican initiative to coordinate Catholic prison ministry
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV created a Vatican service to coordinate Catholic pastoral care for prisoners worldwide, naming Buenos Aires Archbishop Jorge Ignacio García Cuerva as its first coordinator. The office will help local churches organize prison visits, train volunteers and liaise with civil authorities. The move formalizes a priority Leo inherited from Pope Francis and follows Leo’s recent visits to prisons in Equatorial Guinea and Argentina.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV urges major changes after UN climate talks end without agreement
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV expressed concern after UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching agreement, with negotiators divided over whether to address fossil fuels. He said climate-related disasters are increasingly frequent and called for changes in behavior, economic systems and governance. The appeal echoes Pope Francis's environmental focus but does not settle the disputes that blocked consensus at the summit.

articles.title: Poundland collapses into administration, putting 12,000 jobs at risk
articles.summary: Poundland’s directors appointed AlixPartners as administrators after rescue bids failed, putting about 12,000 jobs across 600 UK and Irish stores at risk before Christmas. Stores and distribution centres will remain open while administrators explore a sale of the business or its assets. The retailer has struggled with inflation, competition and funding shortages; the outcome for individual sites and staff remains uncertain.

articles.title: Private capital investment in emerging markets jumps 19% on China tech and infrastructure
articles.summary: Private-capital investment in emerging markets rose 19% through the third quarter to $143.2 billion, the Global Private Capital Association said, driven by Chinese technology funding and infrastructure demand. The total is already close to all of 2025's $158.3 billion. China attracted $64.3 billion, while infrastructure investment also increased in Africa and Central and Eastern Europe. The figures cover reported investment through September, not a full-year forecast.

articles.title: Proposed 2030 census changes could remove race question and add citizenship question
articles.summary: The Census Bureau is considering removing its race-and-ethnicity question and adding a citizenship question to the 2030 census, proposals that civil-rights groups and researchers say could distort population data. Census information guides representation, funding, public-health research and infrastructure planning. Advocates warn a citizenship question could discourage responses in immigrant communities; officials argue alternative data sources exist. The proposals have drawn criticism after the public-comment period closed.

articles.title: Pulitzer-winning composer Caroline Shaw reflects on a career across classical and pop music
articles.summary: Composer, singer and violinist Caroline Shaw discusses a career spanning Pulitzer-winning contemporary music, classical ensembles and collaborations with pop artists including Phoebe Bridgers and Rosalía. The Guardian profile follows her work with the Attacca Quartet and upcoming Barbican residency, while Shaw reflects on the importance of respect, curiosity and enjoying performance rather than treating every project as a relentless cycle. Her schedule remains unusually broad across classical, theatre and pop.

articles.title: Real Madrid beats PSV 5–1 as Arsenal and Manchester City draw in Champions League
articles.summary: Real Madrid recovered from a halftime deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5–1, with Jude Bellingham scoring a standout goal, and kept a perfect Champions League record. Arsenal drew 1–1 with Borussia Dortmund after conceding an equaliser, while Manchester City twice fell behind before drawing 2–2 with Napoli. The results left Madrid top of the league-phase standings, with Arsenal and City dropping points in the fifth matchday.

articles.title: Rory Culkin discusses anxiety, fatherhood and the pressure of acting
articles.summary: In a Guardian interview, actor Rory Culkin discusses anxiety that affected auditions and performances, his decision to stop pushing himself through punishing preparation, and the support he received from his mother and siblings. He also talks about fatherhood and his attraction to darker roles, including his new crime-drama work. The profile offers his own account of a difficult period in his career rather than a broader assessment of Hollywood or mental health.

articles.title: Russia extradites Chinese national wanted over alleged $2.25 billion deposit scheme
articles.summary: Russia has extradited a Chinese national, identified only by the surname Shu, to China, where he is wanted over an alleged scheme involving more than 15 billion yuan ($2.25 billion) in public deposits. Xinhua, citing China’s Ministry of Public Security, said he returned on November 5. Authorities disclosed few details about the alleged fundraising or the extradition process.

articles.title: Russian government official warns of Ukrainian drone attacks on utility infrastructure this winter
articles.summary: Russia’s deputy prime minister said preparing for possible Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian power and heating infrastructure is a top winter priority, especially in border regions. Reuters reported that some facilities near Moscow have anti-drone netting and residents are buying generators and batteries. Last year, attacks near Belgorod left tens of thousands without heat and electricity; Kyiv and Moscow continue to trade strikes on energy sites.

articles.title: Russian strikes target Ukraine's power transmission network, leaving Odesa households without electricity
articles.summary: Russia has increasingly targeted substations and transmission lines that move electricity between Ukrainian regions, rather than only attacking power stations, DTEK's Odesa grid chief told Reuters. He said 60% of regional substations had been struck, some repeatedly. Repairs restored much of the supply, but about 9,000 households remained without power after another overnight attack. Odesa lacks local generation, making its links to western Ukraine especially important.

articles.title: Saudi national kidnapped by suspected Islamic State militants in Niger, sources say
articles.summary: Two security sources told Reuters that suspected Islamic State militants kidnapped a Saudi national in Niger on November 21 or 22 and are holding the person hostage. One source placed the abduction in western Tillaberi, near Mali and Burkina Faso; the other gave a location between Tillaberi and Niamey. No group has claimed responsibility, and Nigerien and Saudi authorities did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court bid to overturn Farmgate panel report
articles.summary: South Africa’s High Court set aside a panel report that said President Cyril Ramaphosa may have breached the constitution in connection with the “Farmgate” scandal. Reuters’ brief report did not detail the court’s reasoning or the practical effect beyond overturning the report. The ruling changes the legal status of the panel’s findings, but it does not by itself resolve every allegation surrounding the affair.

articles.title: Spain and Morocco compete to host the 2030 World Cup final
articles.summary: Spain and Morocco are competing to host the 2030 World Cup final, with Spain’s Bernabéu and Camp Nou facing Morocco’s planned 115,000-seat Hassan II stadium near Casablanca. The contest is complicated by rivalry between Madrid and Barcelona, political tensions and FIFA leadership issues. FIFA has not announced the venue, and inspections of host cities are still underway.

articles.title: Spain election puts housing policy at center of contest over rent caps and construction
articles.summary: Spain’s November 29 election has turned on housing, with conservative leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo promoting Madrid-style deregulation and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez defending Catalonia’s rent caps and limits on short-term lets. Both sides promise more construction, but economists disagree about how supply reforms and rent controls affect prices. The vote could determine which approach becomes national policy.

articles.title: Spain’s climate crisis receives little attention in election debate
articles.summary: Spain’s election debate has given limited attention to climate policy despite recent wildfires and floods, The Guardian reports from a community still recovering from summer fire damage. Experts say voters often rank immediate economic and housing concerns above climate risks, while politicians avoid an issue that can polarize constituencies. The gap raises questions about preparedness and compensation as extreme weather continues to affect the country.

articles.title: Spain's Indra targets rapid defence and space growth through 2035
articles.summary: Spanish defence and technology group Indra set revenue targets above €12 billion by 2030 and €20 billion by 2035, relying on rising European military spending. Its €22 billion order backlog provides visibility, and defence revenue is projected to quadruple to €5.2 billion by 2030. The company also expects space revenue to exceed €1 billion, although its new plan sets a lower 2030 core-profit margin than its previous strategy.

articles.title: SpongeBob SquarePants cast reflects on 27 years as new holiday special arrives
articles.summary: The cast and creators of 'SpongeBob SquarePants' are marking more than 27 years since the series began, ahead of a new holiday special. The animated show remains a major television and merchandise franchise, with more than $17 billion in retail sales and 353 billion minutes watched on YouTube, according to figures cited by AP. Creators credit its mix of humor and family appeal for sustaining multiple generations of fans.

articles.title: Study links GLP-1-associated weight loss with higher breast density and mammogram callbacks
articles.summary: A study of 107 women taking GLP-1 drugs for at least a year found breast density increased after an average 40-pound weight loss, with a 22.4% mammogram recall rate compared with roughly 10% nationally. Four biopsies were benign. Researchers say the change may reflect loss of breast fat rather than more breast tissue; they advise continuing routine screening and telling imaging teams about GLP-1 use and substantial weight loss.

articles.title: Sydney fire-ant colony with multiple queens prompts expanded eradication response
articles.summary: New South Wales officials expanded their response after a red imported fire-ant nest found in Sydney's Auburn suburb proved larger and more complex than first thought. The colony has multiple queens, a form that can support denser nests and is harder to eradicate. Authorities say it is the second Sydney detection this year and are tracing possible supply-chain routes; residents are urged to report sightings rather than disturb nests.

articles.title: Taiwan comedian keeps performing under security after alleged attack plot
articles.summary: Taiwanese comedian Huang Yi-hao continues performing with security present after prosecutors charged five people over an alleged plot to injure him following jokes about China’s leader. Reuters reports Huang was slightly injured when struck by a car in September; investigators allege a Chinese national paid a local man to attack him. Beijing has rejected Taiwan’s accusations of involvement, and the case has become a flashpoint over speech and intimidation.

articles.title: Tata Steel's complex APL Apollo deal draws investor backlash
articles.summary: Tata Steel's proposed combination with Indian steel-tube maker APL Apollo could create a business with 7.5 million metric tons of annual capacity, but the deal structure has angered investors. Tata plans to sell its finished-products unit, buy a major stake from APL Apollo's chair and make a further open offer. A separate manufacturing agreement for the chair's private firm has raised governance concerns, while both companies' shares fell sharply.

articles.title: These young Republicans have a message for their party: It’s time to ‘grow up’
articles.summary: Several dozen young Republicans in Tarrant County, Texas, met after the party’s midterm losses to discuss its direction. Many criticized personal attacks, infighting and limited progress on affordability, while urging stronger leadership and a return to conservative principles. Others favored a harder line. The discussion offers a local snapshot of tensions over Trump’s influence as Republicans look toward 2028.

articles.title: U.S. new home sales jump to 10-month high as builders cut prices
articles.summary: U.S. new single-family home sales rose 14.2% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 701,000, their highest level since December 2025, as builders cut prices to attract buyers. The median price fell 3.2% year over year to $391,300. Higher mortgage rates and elevated unsold inventory remain obstacles, and economists expect housing-market weakness to persist into 2027.

articles.title: U.S. third-quarter GDP growth revised sharply higher to 4.3%
articles.summary: U.S. third-quarter GDP was revised to a 4.3% annualized pace from 3.4%, the fastest in three years. Consumer spending was upgraded to 4.2% and business equipment investment grew 21.8%, much of it tied to AI. Higher-income households drove much of the spending and savings fell, leaving economists watching whether investment and consumption can sustain the pace.

articles.title: UK competition watchdog weighs remedies for proposed $25 billion AkzoNobel-Axalta merger
articles.summary: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority said proposed remedies from AkzoNobel and Axalta could address concerns over their planned $25 billion merger. AkzoNobel offered to sell its European and UK vehicle-refinishing coatings business to preserve competition. The CMA will consult on the proposal and a potential buyer before making a final decision; the regulator previously warned the combined company could hold 40% to 50% of the UK market.

articles.title: UK considers opening BBC iPlayer to advertising and rival broadcasters
articles.summary: Britain is advancing plans to let BBC iPlayer carry content from rival broadcasters and potentially advertising, according to people familiar with the discussions. The changes would require a technology overhaul costing tens of millions of pounds and could be outlined in a government paper on the BBC's charter renewal. The proposal aims to help public-service broadcasters compete with global streaming platforms, but would alter the service's current licence-fee-based model.

articles.title: UK embassy in Japan warns of rise in drink spiking and credit card fraud at Tokyo bars
articles.summary: Britain’s embassy in Tokyo warned visitors about drink-spiking and extortion at nightlife venues in districts including Shinjuku, Roppongi and Shibuya. Police recorded 340 cases in Shinjuku between January and October, 195 more than a year earlier; one alleged charge reached ¥9.6 million. Authorities say foreign tourists are frequent targets, while the true number may be higher because some victims discover fraud only after leaving Japan.

articles.title: UK nuclear test veterans win 40-year battle for inquiry into Cold War tests
articles.summary: Britain has authorized an independent inquiry into the health effects of Cold War nuclear tests witnessed by an estimated 22,000 service members in the Indian and Pacific oceans from 1952 to 1967. Veterans allege exposure and concealed medical testing; the Ministry of Defence's handling of blood records is under scrutiny. Bishop James Jones will chair the panel, which is expected to issue an interim report by October 2027. The UK has no dedicated compensation scheme.

articles.title: UK reportedly moves military aircraft into hangars at night amid drone concerns
articles.summary: Britain's Royal Air Force is moving aircraft into hangars and shelters at night and considering anti-drone netting, according to reports by The Times and Sky News. The Ministry of Defence had not commented. The reports follow warnings from British security agencies about sabotage threats and suspected unauthorised drone activity near military bases, including incidents authorities have linked to possible Iranian involvement.

articles.title: UK watchdog says Colman's sale could ease concerns over $65 billion Unilever deal
articles.summary: Britain’s Competition and Markets Authority said a proposed sale of Unilever’s Colman’s brand could help resolve concerns about McCormick’s planned $65 billion acquisition of Unilever’s food business. The regulator will assess the proposal before deciding whether to clear the deal with conditions or open a deeper investigation. Colman’s makes mustard, sauces and recipe mixes central to the competition review.

articles.title: UK watchdog warns funding uncertainty threatens defence investment plan
articles.summary: Britain’s National Audit Office warned that uncertain funding and underestimated costs threaten delivery of the Defence Investment Plan. The Ministry of Defence has limited assurance it can complete the programme, while planned efficiency savings of nearly £11 billion by 2029–30 are only partly supported by detailed plans. The watchdog also cited reduced training spending and higher costs linked to the Iran war.

articles.title: Ukraine says strike on Russian air base damaged five military aircraft
articles.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck Savasleyka air base in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, damaging three MiG-31 jets and two Su-34 fighter-bombers used in attacks on Ukraine. Russia had not immediately commented, so the reported damage could not be independently confirmed. The strike is part of Kyiv's campaign against Russian military infrastructure as Moscow continues attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy facilities.

articles.title: Underemployment among young U.S. college graduates reaches six-year high
articles.summary: Underemployment among U.S. college graduates aged 22 to 27 reached 42.5% in September, the highest level since 2020, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Many recent graduates are working in roles that do not require degrees or relying on part-time and contract work. Economists cite weak hiring, uncertainty and employers’ use of AI, while noting degrees still tend to improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: US grocers serve up Thanksgiving deals even as turkey prices climb
articles.summary: Major U.S. retailers are offering Thanksgiving meal kits at or below last year's prices to attract inflation-weary shoppers, even as wholesale turkey and potato costs rise. Reuters reported frozen whole-turkey prices reached record highs, while grocers absorb some of the increase to signal value. Walmart's 26-item meal kit costs $35 for ten people, five dollars less than last year. Retailers hope shoppers add higher-margin extras.

articles.title: US inflation accelerates again in October as Fed rate-hike expectations grow
articles.summary: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose 0.3% in October and 3.8% over the year, while core inflation reached 3.3%, according to government data. Consumer spending also increased, supported largely by higher-income households. Financial markets are pricing in another Federal Reserve rate increase in December and possibly January. Persistent inflation is eroding wage gains and may slow household spending as 2027 approaches.

articles.title: US jobless claims fall to 189,000, pointing to a steady labour market
articles.summary: New US applications for unemployment benefits fell by 13,000 to 189,000 in the week ending November 21, below economists' expectations. Continuing claims also declined, suggesting layoffs remain limited even as hiring is subdued. The figures were released a day early because of Thanksgiving. A stable labour market could give the Federal Reserve more room to keep raising rates as it tries to bring inflation back toward its 2% target.

articles.title: US orders for core business equipment rise more than expected in October
articles.summary: Orders for US-made non-defence capital goods excluding aircraft rose 1.2% in October, beating economists' expectations and extending a run of strong business-equipment investment. Shipments also increased, supporting the equipment-spending component of GDP. AI infrastructure investment has helped drive recent growth, but investors are questioning the cost and returns of data-centre expansion. Durable-goods orders rose more modestly as weaker aircraft orders offset gains elsewhere.

articles.title: US-Mexico intelligence cooperation may ease tensions after cartel leader's capture
articles.summary: Mexico's arrest of Sinaloa-linked figure Fausto Isidro Meza Flores followed months of planning and U.S. intelligence support, including a surveillance drone deployed at Mexico's request. Analysts told AP the operation could offer a model for cooperation without U.S. troops operating on Mexican soil. Tensions remain over sovereignty and extradition: Washington seeks custody, while Mexico says he will face prosecution there first.

articles.title: US-sought activist Fergie Chambers says extradition case should not punish his political beliefs
articles.summary: James 'Fergie' Chambers, a U.S. citizen sought for extradition by Washington over allegations linked to support for Hamas and protest activity, told The Guardian he fears being targeted for his political views. A Spanish court released him on bail after identifying problems with translations in the U.S. request; proceedings are paused while the issue is reviewed. Chambers denies wrongdoing, and any extradition remains unresolved as he pursues asylum in Spain.

articles.title: Walmart-backed PhonePe restarts IPO plans at up to $15 billion valuation
articles.summary: Indian digital-payments company PhonePe has resumed preparations for an initial public offering and is targeting a $12 billion to $15 billion valuation in early 2027, a source told Reuters. The proposed sale could raise $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion, mainly allowing Walmart and other investors to reduce or exit holdings. PhonePe has more than 650 million registered users and processed nearly half of India's UPI transactions in October.

articles.title: Walmart-owned Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down
articles.summary: Walmart-owned Flipkart said chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy will leave after more than 11 years leading the Indian e-commerce group. The company says product and technology chief Balaji Thiagarajan will run the business temporarily while a successor is selected. Flipkart has more than 500 million registered users and has long prepared for a possible public listing, though no timetable was announced.

articles.title: With new league in planning stages, NBA announces $11B initiative for arena development in Europe
articles.summary: The NBA announced an initiative targeting at least €10 billion (nearly $11 billion) from global investors to build or modernize arenas and related entertainment districts across Europe. The financing is intended to support clubs in a planned NBA-FIBA league expected to begin next fall. Potential markets include Britain, France, Spain, Italy, Germany, Greece and Turkey, but no participating cities have been selected.

articles.title: Wolf comeback divides the densely populated Netherlands
articles.summary: Wolves, absent from the Netherlands for about two centuries, have returned in growing numbers, but their recovery has sparked conflict in the densely populated country. Researchers estimate fewer than 150 animals in about 15 packs, while farmers report thousands of livestock losses. The government says it plans to permit some culling to prevent attacks; conservationists argue coexistence measures remain essential.

articles.title: Yemenis prepare to flee as Houthis advance toward Aden
articles.summary: Residents and aid groups in Aden are preparing for possible evacuation as Houthi forces mass north and east of the city, roughly 50 miles away, and could cut key roads. The Houthis have not declared an immediate assault, but a siege or capture would sharply weaken Yemen’s Saudi-backed government. The advance compounds a humanitarian emergency: 18.7 million people face acute food insecurity and more than 350,000 have been displaced since August.

articles.title: CDC reports nine verified measles-related deaths in the U.S. in 2026 as tallies diverge
articles.summary: The CDC counted nine verified measles-related deaths in the United States in 2026 and 6,039 confirmed cases across 47 jurisdictions through Nov. 24. Public state reports, however, imply at least 14 associated deaths, exposing a gap between federal and state tallies after the CDC changed its verification method. The agency said 11% of patients were hospitalized, with the highest rate among children under five, and warned totals may change.

articles.title: India says U.S. deported 1,700 Indian nationals so far in 2026
articles.summary: India’s foreign ministry said the United States deported 1,700 Indian nationals between January and Nov. 25, below the 3,567 recorded in 2025 but up from 1,273 reported through July 2026. The ministry says it verifies each person’s nationality before accepting returns. It provided no monthly breakdown, and the figures exclude people merely identified for removal or still in immigration proceedings.

articles.title: Todoist says breach exposed email addresses and legacy password hashes for 6% of users
articles.summary: Todoist says a stolen credential let an intruder alter development workflows and reach its cloud production environment on Nov. 22–23. About 6% of users had email addresses, account dates and older salted-SHA1 password hashes exposed; roughly 0.001% had task or comment content searched for credentials. API and Slack tokens were also accessed. The company says it blocked the path, reset affected credentials and disabled the Outlook add-on.

articles.title: Allstate outage leaves customers unable to access policies and claims before Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Allstate’s website and mobile app remained unavailable for multiple days before Thanksgiving, leaving customers unable to review policies, pay bills, submit claims or use app-based roadside assistance. TechCrunch reported the outage began Monday and affected customers nationwide. The insurer had not publicly explained the cause or provided a restoration timeline, forcing some customers to contact local agents by phone or email.

articles.title: Hera spacecraft reveals crater and boulders on asteroid struck by NASA
articles.summary: Europe’s Hera mission released the first close-up images of Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA’s DART spacecraft struck in 2022. The images show a stadium-sized flattened crater, chaotic tumbling and hundreds of orbiting boulders. DART shortened Dimorphos’s orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes; Hera’s follow-up measurements will help scientists understand how asteroid structure affects deflection and improve future planetary-defense planning.

articles.title: BNP Paribas moves into higher global systemic-bank category, raising capital buffer
